title: The ratified primary estimator's omitted category is day −14, not day −1; day −1 is deleted from the sample entirely
fix: Keep the day −1 rows in the estimation sample and make −1 the omitted level explicitly — e.g. `C(rel_day, Treatment(reference=-1))`, or build integer-coded event-time dummies and drop the −1 column by name. Then assert in code that the set of estimated rel_days equals the window minus {−1}. Better still for a design with this much window truncation: use a pre-period average (−14..−2) as the baseline rather than any single day, and say which in the caption.
claim: `event_study.fit_event_study` removes the reference-day rows from the data (`d = stack[stack["rel_day"] != EVENT_REFERENCE_DAY]`, scripts/event_study.py:59) and then fits `C(rel_day)`. Formulaic drops the *lowest remaining* level as the base, which is rel_day = −14. So `EVENT_REFERENCE_DAY = -1` (scripts/config.py:122) is inert: day −1 is not the baseline, it is discarded, and every event-time coefficient — including the H1 test statistic — is measured against a single day two weeks before the episode.
corrected_claim:
The claim is correct as stated, with two refinements.

(1) Citation nit: `EVENT_REFERENCE_DAY = -1` is at scripts/config.py:123, not :122.

(2) Scope correction on impact: the finding implies the whole H1 result is compromised. Verified, it is narrower. Because `placebo_starts` draws preserve episode spacing and the same `fit_event_study` runs on each draw, the omitted level is -14 in 39/39 placebo draws I ran (27 coefficients every time), so the randomization-inference p-value — the ratified primary inference — is still a valid test of the sharp null. What is actually broken is: (a) the reported `first_week_effect` point estimate, which is the mean day-0..7 level minus the level on the single day -14 rather than relative to the pre-period or to day -1; (b) its sampling variance, which absorbs all of day -14's noise plus any 14-day drift or within-window seasonality not soaked up by the ep_cd and dow fixed effects; (c) the identification asymmetry — 17 of 30 episodes reach day -14 versus 25 at day 0, so baseline and treated days come from different episode sets; (d) Figure 2's stated reference period (PAPER_PLAN.md:204-207) and the scripts/17_stacked_event_study.py:13-15 docstring, both of which assert day -1 and are wrong.

Note also that data/processed/panel_cd_day.parquet does not exist in the repo, so neither this audit nor the original could run the estimator on real outcomes; both reproductions are on a synthetic panel with the real frozen episode dates. The omitted-category behaviour is a property of the formula and the row filter, not of the outcome values, so it carries over — but the 17/25 episode counts are a property of `build_stack` truncation on the real episode spacing (gaps of 7, 8, 9, 7 and 14 days between consecutive discovery episodes), and those are real.

The proposed fix is correct. `C(rel_day, Treatment(reference=EVENT_REFERENCE_DAY))` on the un-filtered stack, plus an assertion that the estimated rel_day set equals the window minus {-1}, is the minimal correct change; a pre-period average baseline is the better design given how much of the pre-window is truncated away.

title: Randomization inference — the ratified primary p-value — builds its null from placebo designs with roughly half the real number of episodes, inflating the null SD ~1.5×
fix: Draw placebo start sets of exactly the same cardinality as the real set. Either (a) circular-shift the whole episode date vector with wrap-around — what scripts/04_robustness.py:72-82 already does correctly for the continuous measure, preserving both count and spacing — or (b) keep the anchor-plus-gaps walk but wrap dates modulo the window and reject any draw that does not yield len(real_starts) episodes. Then re-derive every RI p-value and re-run the calibration.
claim: `placebo_starts` (scripts/event_study.py:100-122) draws one uniform anchor in [lo+pre, hi−post] and then walks forward through a permutation of the real gaps, breaking as soon as a date passes `latest` (:118-121). Because the real episodes span nearly the whole window, the gaps sum to nearly the whole window, so a mid-range anchor loses about half the episodes. The null distribution is generated by a smaller design than the observed one, and a smaller design has a wider sampling distribution, so the reported p-value is systematically too large.
corrected_claim: Confirmed as stated, with two numeric refinements and one addition. Refinements: the all-70-episode placebo mean is 37.1, not 37.6 (depends on assumed panel bounds); and in my reproduction the absolute SDs are 0.001155 (30 episodes) versus 0.001835 (shipped placebo draws, mean 16.6 episodes), a 1.59x inflation rather than the claimed 0.000972/0.001502 and 1.55x — different absolute scale from a different seed, same ratio and same conclusion. Addition: the null-calibration gate meant to catch exactly this failure cannot. scripts/18_null_calibration.py:127-131 tests the rejection rate against a symmetric binomial interval that, at the 12 sims actually run, is (-0.0733, 0.1733); the committed outputs/tables/null_calibration.csv therefore records empirical_rejection_rate = 0.0 and median_p = 0.7142 — textbook under-rejection — and still prints VERDICT: CALIBRATED. The fix must therefore cover both files: draw placebo sets of exactly len(real_starts) (circular shift with wrap-around, as scripts/04_robustness.py:72-76 already does for the continuous measure), and make script 18's verdict test the whole p-value distribution for uniformity (e.g. KS or a two-sided check on median p) rather than only the tail rate against an interval that admits zero.

title: Flipping FREEZE_ACTIVE alone pools the discovery episodes into the confirmatory sample — and with the sample dates unchanged, silently runs on discovery data while reporting 70 episodes
fix: Add a CONFIRMATION_EPISODES = "extension" config switch consumed by 17 and 07 so the confirmatory run is extension-only by default, with any pooled run reported separately and labelled. Couple the sample window to the freeze (derive ANALYSIS_START/END from FREEZE_ACTIVE, or assert every episode passed in yields a non-empty window). Write the realised episode count (stack["episode"].nunique()) to the results table beside the requested one and fail loudly when they differ.
claim: scripts/17_stacked_event_study.py:86-87 restricts to `period == "discovery"` only while the freeze holds; once `FREEZE_ACTIVE = False` the estimator uses all 70 episodes, so the confirmatory H1 test is computed on a sample in which 30 of 70 episodes are the ones the test statistic was selected on (GATE_C_MEMO.md §1 chooses joint lags 0-7 over days 3-5 by comparing their discovery p-values: 0.041/0.006 versus 0.407/0.293). CONFIRMATION_PLAN.md:4-5 defines the confirmation package as the extension plus independent outcomes, not the pooled decade. Compounding this, GATE_C_MEMO.md §6.6 item C records that ANALYSIS_START/END are still discovery-scoped, and nothing in the code couples the two switches.
corrected_claim: Confirmed with three refinements. Flipping FREEZE_ACTIVE alone (scripts/config.py:137) removes the `period == "discovery"` filter at scripts/17_stacked_event_study.py:86-87 but leaves ANALYSIS_START/END at 2017-01-01..2020-12-31 (config.py:34-35), so build_stack is handed 70 starts and only 31 realise a window (episode ids 19..49, n_obs 36049 versus 35636 under the freeze); the other 39 are dropped silently at scripts/event_study.py:29-30, while line 126 writes n_episodes = 70 into event_study_results.csv and the banner prints "episodes in scope: 70 (all)". REFINEMENT 1: the 31st episode is id 49 (2021-01-06, extension), truncated to 2020-12-24..2020-12-31, so it contributes 8 pre-period days (rel_day -13..-6) and ZERO day-0..7 observations — the estimate is discovery-only in substance, not merely discovery-dominated. REFINEMENT 2: GATE_C_MEMO.md:290 item C covers PANEL_BUFFER_START/END as well, and scripts/01_build_panel.py:44,79 builds the panel only over 2016-12-01..2021-01-31, so widening ANALYSIS_START/END alone would still admit no extension data without rebuilding the panel; the "silently discovery-only mislabelled as 70 episodes" branch is therefore the near-certain outcome and the "pooled decade" branch requires two further edits. REFINEMENT 3: the randomization-inference episode-count mismatch is real but is NOT caused by the flip — with seed 20260908 and 2000 draws, placebo_starts yields mean 15.51 episodes from the 70-gap vector against 31 observed, but the same simulation under the ACTIVE freeze yields mean 16.21 against 30 observed, so this is a pre-existing defect in scripts/event_study.py:100-122 and should be reported separately rather than as a compounding consequence. The selection evidence is exact: GATE_C_MEMO.md:26-27 chooses joint lags 0-7 (p = 0.041 / 0.006) over days 3-5 (p = 0.407 / 0.293) on discovery data, while CONFIRMATION_PLAN.md:4-5 and GATE_C_MEMO.md:279 define the confirmatory sample as the 40 extension episodes. The proposed fix (an explicit CONFIRMATION_EPISODES switch, coupling the sample window to the freeze, and writing the realised stack["episode"].nunique() beside the requested count with a loud failure on mismatch) is correct as stated.

title: All three ratified validation gates are constructed so that they cannot fail
fix: (a) Replace the verdict rule with a one-sided test in which a rejection rate below nominal fails, clamp lo at 0, require enough RI draws that p < alpha is attainable (>= 200) and enough sims for an informative interval (>= 500), and add a KS test of p-value uniformity. Re-run after fixing placebo_starts. (b) Validate the crosswalk against something external — precinct population or the published B-HEARD precinct call counts — not against a discovery regression it cannot affect. (c) Re-derive divergence days on a fixed CAI-S component set and report how many survive in 2017-2020; if none, drop the test from the display-item list and say why.
claim: Gate C ratified three checks as preconditions on the confirmatory run; none can return a failure. (a) Synthetic-null calibration: `calibrated = lo <= rej <= hi` with `lo = alpha − 1.96·sqrt(alpha(1−alpha)/n_sims)` (scripts/18_null_calibration.py:129-131) — at the n_sims actually run, lo is negative, so zero rejections passes. (b) B-HEARD discovery-invariance: exposure is identically 0 on every discovery day by construction (asserted at scripts/16_bheard_exposure.py:212-215), so adding it to a 2017-2020 model adds a column of zeros and cannot move any estimate however wrong the crosswalk is. (c) CAI-S divergence-day falsification: its sample contains zero discovery-window days, and its membership is a GDELT-availability artifact rather than genuine supply/demand divergence.
corrected_claim:
Two of the three gates are vacuous exactly as described; the third has a meaningless stored verdict but for the opposite reason given, and the "cannot fail by construction" framing is wrong for it.

CONFIRMED (b) — B-HEARD discovery-invariance validates nothing about the crosswalk. data/reference/bheard_cd_exposure.csv has 74 rows (30 CDs x 2 bounds), min effective_from 2021-06-01, zero rows before 2021 (2021:8, 2022:21, 2023:35, 2024:10). Exposure is identically 0 over 2017-2020 by construction (scripts/16_bheard_exposure.py:22 docstring, assert at :211-215). GATE_C_MEMO.md:120-121 states the check verbatim as "adding the control must leave the 2017-2020 discovery results numerically unchanged. If they move, the crosswalk is wrong." A constant-zero regressor cannot move any 2017-2020 estimate however wrong the precinct->CD call-volume weights are. Correction: it is not the only check in the codebase — scripts/16 also asserts the IBO operational-count brackets (:230-235, validates adoption DATES) and a step-table/crosswalk round-trip (:252-256, internal consistency). Neither validates the weights against anything external, so PAPER_PLAN.md:269 (RECORD 12.3, "linkage quality evaluation") remains unmet.

CONFIRMED (c) — divergence-day sample is a GDELT-availability artifact. Re-derived from data/processed/cai_daily.parquet with the rule at scripts/12_build_cai.py:147-149: exactly 18 days, {2015:11, 2016:3, 2021:1, 2023:3}, zero in 2017-2020. 17 of 18 (94.4%) have only gdelt_tv available, against a 38.7% single-component base rate (1384/3572) in the eligible sample; gdelt_news spans only 2017-01-01 to 2022-12-31. GATE_C_MEMO.md:307 cites the 18-day sample as evidence the two-tier design "is doing real work."

PARTLY WRONG (a) — the stored calibration verdict is meaningless, but not because the test is conservative by construction, and not because the rule cannot fail. Facts reproduce: n_sims_completed=12, ri_draws_per_sim=25, ar1_rho=0.6, empirical_rejection_rate=0.0, acceptable_range_lo=-0.0733, hi=0.1733, median_p=0.7142, VERDICT=CALIBRATED; 12 p-values mean 0.630, 11 of 12 above 0.37, min 0.0833. data/processed/ has no panel_cd_day.parquet, so the calibration branch (scripts/18_null_calibration.py:68-81) never ran and rho=0.6, sigma=0.03, mu=0.10 are assumed defaults — the run does not satisfy GATE_C_MEMO.md:257-259. The script does not misrepresent this; it branches and prints "real panel not built yet."
Two corrections. (1) The arithmetic is inverted. p = k/n with the observed statistic EXCLUDED (scripts/event_study.py:141), so at 25 draws both k=0 (p=0.0) and k=1 (p=0.04) reject; rejection does not require beating all 25 draws, and nominal P(reject) under exchangeability is 2/26 = 7.7%, i.e. anti-conservative rather than the claimed 3.8% conservative ceiling. The effective denominators are not even 25 — the stored p-values are 1/2, 3/4, 5/6, 3/8, 1/12, 22/23, 17/24 and k/25, and at n=2 the null rejection probability is 1/3. The RI test is under-powered and erratically sized, not conservative by construction.
(2) The rule can fail. VERDICT flips to NOT CALIBRATED whenever rej > 0.1733 (3+ of 12 sims), and lo turns positive at n >= 73 completed sims; at the documented default --sims 200, lo = +0.0198 and a 0.0 rejection rate would FAIL. The genuine defect is that se is computed from len(pvals) (scripts/18_null_calibration.py:129) with no minimum-sims floor, so a 12-sim run widens its own acceptance band into passing.
Net effect on the decision: unchanged for (b) and (c) — both gates should be replaced before the confirmatory run. For (a) the fix is different from the one proposed: the rule does not need to become one-sided against under-rejection (that direction is not the failure mode present); it needs a minimum-sims precondition, per-sim minimum valid-draw counts (the variable denominators, traceable to placebo_starts returning short sequences at scripts/event_study.py:107-120), and a uniformity test of the p-values, then a re-run at the documented defaults.

title: The frozen episode list applies a fixed level threshold to an index whose location and scale drift by a factor of three, so "an attention episode" means something different in every year
fix: Define episodes on a within-period standardized index (rolling 365-day z, or year-demeaned and year-scaled), or equivalently on a within-year quantile, so "episode" has constant meaning across 2015-2024; then report episodes per year as a design diagnostic and require it to be roughly flat. Drop 2015-01..2015-06 as DATA_AUDIT.md §3 already recommends but the frozen list has not implemented. Publish the per-year before/after counts alongside the episode diff (DATA_AUDIT.md §6 step 4).
claim: Episodes are runs of days with `cai_d > 1.0` (scripts/config.py:96; scripts/13_extension_episodes.py:23). CAI-D is a mean of separately standardized components (scripts/12_build_cai.py:74-84) standardized on 2017-2019 only (:39), so it is neither unit-variance nor mean-zero outside that window. The fixed 1.0 cut therefore corresponds to wildly different attention percentiles across the sample. This is the project's known error class applied to the object the pre-registration actually froze — and the fix DATA_AUDIT.md §1 proposes does not remove it, because it addresses scale and not level.
corrected_claim:
The frozen episode rule applies a fixed level cut (`cai_d > 1.0`, scripts/config.py:96, scripts/13_extension_episodes.py:23) to an index that is neither unit-variance nor mean-zero anywhere — including inside its own anchor window. Because scripts/12_build_cai.py:74-84 averages separately-standardized components rather than standardizing the composite, CAI-D has mean -0.0062 and SD 0.6505 on 2017-2019, so the cut is 1.55 reference-window SD, not 1. Across years the same cut is 0.80 / 1.05 / 1.50 / 1.62 / 1.54 / 0.05 / 1.63 / 2.31 / 1.94 / 3.60 within-year SD (2015-2024), producing 81/35/28/19/24/139/19/16/16/1 high days. Within-year SD ranges 0.436 to 1.377, a factor of 3.2.

The consequence is that episodes are not comparable objects. It shows up in episode LENGTH and intensity, not in episode count: 2015 and 2022 both yield 12 episodes, but 2015's cover 81 high days (mean 6.75 days, mean peak 1.78) while 2022's cover 16 (mean 1.33 days, 9 of 12 single-day, mean peak 1.28). Across all 70 episodes, 34 are single high days with median peak 1.13. scripts/17_stacked_event_study.py:85-111 enters every episode start as one identically-weighted event with no intensity weighting, so a 1.02 blip and the 43-day, peak-3.93 Freddie Gray window count the same.

The defect is not confined to the frozen extension list: in 2020 the cut sits at 0.05 within-year SD and flags 139 of 366 days, so the already-examined discovery sample is affected too (compounding the 128-day episode 45 that DATA_AUDIT.md §4 flags).

Rebuilding as DATA_AUDIT.md §1 recommends does not fix cross-year meaning drift: the three always-on components, restandardized after averaging with the threshold re-derived on 2017-19, still give 2 high days in 2024 against 59-84 in 2017-2019. (The corresponding 2015 figure is implementation-sensitive — 109 if days missing wiki_ext are tolerated, 32 if the component set is held strictly fixed — so the late-sample collapse, not the 2015 excess, is the robust part.)

Separately confirmed: wiki_ext begins 2015-07-01, and 8 of the 40 extension episodes start before it. Episode 6 (2015-04-01..2015-05-29, 43 high days, peak 3.93), the Freddie Gray / Walter Scott window CONFIRMATION_PLAN.md:23 names as a target event, is built from trends_us, trends_nyc and trends_victims only — i.e. from Google Trends alone.

NOT supported: the assertion that episode density is lowest in 2022-24 and therefore correlated with B-HEARD exposure. 2022 has 12 episodes, tied with 2015 for the most; only 2023 (5), 2021 (4) and 2024 (1) are low, and the series is non-monotone.

Fix: define episodes on a within-period standardized index (rolling 365-day z, or year-demeaned and year-scaled) or a within-year quantile; report episodes-per-year AND high-days-per-episode as design diagnostics; drop 2015-01..06 as DATA_AUDIT.md §3 already recommends; publish per-year before/after counts with the episode diff (DATA_AUDIT.md §6 step 4). Note that this correction, unlike a pure rescaling, changes the discovery-period event set as well, so any re-run must be reported against the existing 2017-2020 results rather than silently replacing them.

title: The estimator ratified as primary has no control group, no calendar controls, non-clustered CIs, and discards all dose variation — while the only design with a control group has a contaminated control set
fix: Add calendar controls to the stacked design (episode×district FE plus day-of-week plus at minimum month-of-year, or a within-window linear trend) and report a dose-weighted version where each episode enters with its peak CAI-D. Cluster the event-time path by date or by episode rather than `hetero`, and state which in the Figure 2 caption. Make the treated and control sets disjoint by construction — drop districts in both, or define the control as bottom-quartile Herfindahl among non-top-quartile-Black districts — and write realised group sizes to the results table. Report the DID and heterogeneity estimates as co-primary, since they are the only estimates with a comparison group.
claim: The stacked event study fits `y ~ C(rel_day) | ep_cd + dow` with `vcov="hetero"` (scripts/event_study.py:57-68; scripts/17_stacked_event_study.py:111). There is no month, year or calendar FE and no untreated comparison unit — treatment is citywide, so all 59 districts are treated simultaneously. Identification is a raw before/after contrast inside 29-day windows, so anything citywide moving on a 29-day scale (season, weather, holidays, COVID waves, protest activity) is in the estimate. Treatment is also reduced to a binary threshold crossing, discarding the intensity variation the secondary distributed-lag model (scripts/03_main_model.py, which does carry month_year FE) actually uses. Meanwhile the exposure DID — the one design with cross-sectional identification — assigns three districts to both arms.
corrected_claim:
The primary stacked event study fits `y ~ C(rel_day) | ep_cd + dow` (scripts/event_study.py:57,66; scripts/17_stacked_event_study.py:111) with no untreated comparison unit, and reduces a highly skewed treatment to a binary episode indicator. Episode 45 (Floyd/Brooks, 2020-05-26..2020-10-01, peak CAI-D 5.36) contains 113 of the 210 discovery high days (53.8%) and its 129 calendar days are 8.8% of discovery days but 55.9% of CAI-D variance (2020 overall: 25.1% of days, 62.6% of variance) — yet in the stack it contributes 25 district-days per district, the same order as a single-day episode. The FE structure already absorbs episode-level calendar variation (ep_cd is episode x district) and day-of-week; what is missing is a within-window trend or seasonal control, so 29-day-scale citywide movement that is systematically aligned with episode starts remains in the point estimate, and 18_null_calibration.py cannot detect it because its synthetic panels contain only district FE + dow FE + AR(1) district noise, no citywide or seasonal component.

The inference critique as originally stated is wrong. The reported p-value for H1 is episode-level randomization inference over 2000 placebo draws (17_stacked_event_study.py:26-34, 121-127; event_study.py:96-127; GATE_C_MEMO §6.3), adopted precisely because clustered SEs proved anti-conservative on this data; it is more conservative than the proposed date-clustering, not less. The `vcov="hetero"` SEs appear only in event_study_path.csv, which no script in the repository reads: the figure actually coded as Figure 2 (08_figures.py:93-109) uses irf_main.csv with `se_date_cluster` and says so in its title. If event_study_path.csv is later used for a coefficient plot, its hetero SEs must be replaced with date- or episode-clustered ones — but that is a forward-looking hygiene item, not a defect in a produced result.

The concrete, code-confirmed defect is in the DID. With the quartiles as coded (07_did_exposure.py:45-48,55), districts 111, 314 and 414 fall in both the top-quartile-%Black treated set and the bottom-quartile-Herfindahl primary control set; line :86 resolves them to treated, so the primary DID is 15 treated vs 12 control, while line :94 writes n_control_cds = len(ctrl_cds) = 15. The results table therefore overstates the primary control group by 3 of 15. Fix: make the sets disjoint by construction and write realised group sizes. The q2_black sensitivity arm has no overlap and is sound.

title: The "clean control window" rule deletes the event windows of exactly the closest-spaced, highest-attention episodes, and the guard meant to catch this cannot fire
fix: Stop deleting overlapping days; assign each district-day to its nearest episode, or fit one model with episode-specific event-time dummies that permits shared control days. Exclude pre-window days falling inside any episode's high-attention span rather than only those before the next episode's start, and report how many that removes. Enforce a per-episode inclusion rule (an episode enters only if it has day −1 and at least k of days 0..7), report contributing episodes per rel_day in the results table, and apply the same rule inside the RI draws.
claim: `build_stack` truncates each window at the next episode's start and then drops any district-day claimed by more than one window (scripts/event_study.py:24-40). When two episodes are less than 28 days apart — which is when attention is most sustained — the overlap is removed from both, so the earlier episode loses its post-window and the later one loses its pre-window. The rule truncates only on the next episode's start, never excluding pre-window days that fall inside a preceding episode's high-attention span, so "clean control" days are routinely days when attention was still elevated. `MIN_FIRST_WEEK_DAYS = 6` (scripts/event_study.py:75, :92-95), which the docstring says exists to keep the statistic's composition constant across draws, counts globally identified coefficients rather than per-episode coverage, so it never binds.
corrected_claim: build_stack (scripts/event_study.py:24-40) truncates each window at the next episode's start and drops any district-day claimed by two windows, so episodes spaced less than pre+post (28) days apart lose window days at both ends. This is real and heavily unbalances the panel: on the 30 frozen discovery episodes only 9 have a complete -14..+14 window, 5 contribute none of days 0..7, mean first-week coverage is 6.3 of 8 days, and episodes per rel_day run from 17 (at -14) to 25 (at day 0), so each day-0..7 coefficient averaged by first_week_effect is identified from a different episode subset than the -14 base. MIN_FIRST_WEEK_DAYS = 6 counts globally identified coefficients, not per-episode coverage, and in 1,940 placebo draws it never once fell below 8 — the guard cannot fire, so the comment at scripts/event_study.py:71-75 describes a protection that does not exist. Two parts of the original claim do not survive checking. First, contamination of control days is marginal, not routine: after truncation and dedup only 8 of 277 surviving pre-window district-days (2.9%), in 4 of 30 episodes, fall inside an episode's high-attention span, and Floyd keeps just one (2020-05-16), because the dedup already removes 2020-05-12..15. Second, the selection runs opposite to the direction claimed: coverage correlates POSITIVELY with intensity (corr(days 0..7, peak_cai_d) = +0.138; mean peak 1.687 for full-week episodes vs 1.359 for partial), and every high-intensity episode — Floyd 5.36, Clark 2.62, Wallace 2.55 — retains a complete first week, so the surviving sample is if anything tilted toward high-attention episodes, not away. Separately and more seriously, fit_event_study drops rel_day == -1 rows from the estimation sample instead of omitting -1 as a reference level, making rel_day = -14 the de facto base and contradicting scripts/17_stacked_event_study.py:52-54; and placebo_starts truncates its date chain at `latest`, producing placebo stacks averaging 16.05 episodes against the observed 30 — a far bigger observed/placebo mismatch than window truncation causes.

title: Randomization-inference null is built from placebo designs with half as many episodes as the real one
fix: Constrain placebo draws to designs with the same number of events as the real one: draw the anchor from [earliest, latest - sum(gaps)] so all N starts always fit (or wrap circularly within the analysis window), and reject any draw yielding n != len(real_starts). Additionally exclude placebo starts falling within +/-14 days of a real episode start, since nothing currently prevents a "null" draw from landing on a real attention spike. Then extend 18_null_calibration.py's acceptance criterion to test uniformity (KS), not just the rejection rate, and re-run with the default 200 sims rather than the 12 recorded.
claim: `placebo_starts` (scripts/event_study.py:100-122) draws a uniform anchor in [lo+pre+1, hi-post-1] and then walks forward through the permuted real gaps, breaking as soon as a start would exceed `latest` (lines 118-120). The real 30 discovery starts span 1,324 days inside a ~1,430-day admissible interval, so all 30 fit only if the anchor lands in the first ~7% of the interval. The null distribution the primary p-value is read off is therefore generated by a *different estimator* (fewer events, noisier statistic) than the observed statistic.
corrected_claim: The claim is correct as stated, with two factual refinements. (1) Magnitude: the finding's own sqrt(30/16) = 1.37 inflation figure understates the damage. Measured directly on script 18's synthetic generator, the current null has SD 0.002109 against 0.001197 for a null constrained to all 30 episodes — a ratio of 1.76 — because short placebo designs lose fixed-effect precision on top of the 1/sqrt(n) term. In p-value terms, a statistic at the true 95th percentile of the correct null is reported as p = 0.223, and one at the true 99th percentile as p = 0.134; the primary p-value is inflated roughly 4.5x at alpha = 0.05. (2) Status: data/processed/panel_cd_day.parquet does not exist and outputs/tables/event_study_results.csv has never been written, so script 17 has not been run and no confirmatory p has been reported yet. The finding is therefore a precondition blocker on the confirmatory run, not an invalidation of a published number — which is if anything better news, since it can be fixed before the freeze is lifted. Everything else reproduces exactly: mean 16.21 / median 16 placebo episodes vs 30 real, 92.0% of draws short, 3.0% silently discarded by the len(ps) < 2 guard, only 7.4% of anchors admit all 30, KS-vs-uniform p = 0.2127 on the 12 recorded calibration p-values, and 48.8% of placebo starts landing within +/-14 days of a real episode start. The proposed fix (anchor in [earliest, latest - sum(gaps)] so n is always 30, reject n != len(real_starts), exclude placebo starts near real episodes, and add a uniformity test to 18_null_calibration.py's acceptance criterion with the default 200 sims rather than the 12 x 25 draws recorded) is the right remedy.

title: The 14-day attribution lookback is shorter than the death-to-attention lag, so the largest non-2020 episode is attributed to the wrong deaths
fix: Widen the attribution lookback to at least 60 days and rank candidates by post-episode Wikipedia pageviews rather than by date proximity, so video-release-driven spikes attach to the right death. Separately audit the registry for known omissions (Prude) before the labels are used in print, and state explicitly that non-police killings such as Neely cannot be captured by an MPV-derived registry.
claim: scripts/13_extension_episodes.py:40 searches for candidate events in [start - 14 days, end]. Attention to police killings is frequently triggered by video release, indictment or verdict weeks after the death, so the window systematically excludes the actual cause of the spike for exactly the high-attention episodes that matter most.
corrected_claim:
The attribution mechanism is broken, but the 14-day lookback is not the binding cause and two pieces of the offered evidence do not reproduce.

CONFIRMED: scripts/13_extension_episodes.py:40 windows candidates to [start-14d, end] and :41 ranks them by tweet_volume with .fillna(0). Episode 65 (2023-01-26 to 2023-02-09, peak cai_d 4.0756 on 2023-01-28) is labelled "David Lawrence Couch III; Bradley S. Havermale", both of whom died on 2023-02-09, the episode's end date. Tyre Nichols is in data/reference/victim_registry.csv at 2023-01-07, five days before the window opens on 2023-01-12, and has no row in wikipedia_article_resolution.csv. The episode is a genuine attention event — all four components spike together on 2023-01-27/28 (gdelt_tv 5.20, trends_nyc 3.25, trends_us 2.81, trends_victims 2.92) — so only the label is wrong. Daniel Prude is absent from the registry (no Rochester NY entry in 2020-03/04) and Jordan Neely is absent; episode 67 (2023-05-04 to 2023-05-11, immediately after Neely's 2023-05-03 death) is labelled "Robert Joseph Layton; Justin Roberts". docs/CONFIRMATION_PLAN.md:23-25 is cited correctly.

CORRECTED (1): episode 65's peak of 4.08 is NOT "the largest peak in the entire sample outside 2020". 2016-07-08 = 5.1456, 2016-07-07 = 4.5485 and 2016-07-09 = 4.2993 all exceed it. It is the second-largest non-2020 episode peak, behind episode 15 (Sterling/Castile).

CORRECTED (2): "cai_d peaks at 2.44 on 2020-09-04" is wrong as stated. The value is right (2.4375) but it is not a local peak — 2020-08-27 = 2.7209 and 2020-09-03 = 2.6018 are higher — and it lies inside episode 45 (2020-05-26 to 2020-10-01), so Prude's absence from the registry changes no episode label. That example does not support the lookback claim; it supports only the separate registry-omission point.

CORRECTED (3), and this is the substantive correction: the proposed fix does not work, because the lookback is not the binding constraint. Re-running episode 65's attribution at 60 and 120 days returns the identical top-2 (['David Lawrence Couch III', 'Bradley S. Havermale'], max p = 0.0). Nichols enters the window at 60 days and still cannot be selected. The actual defect is the ranking key: tweet_volume is inherited from the retired Twitter measure and has effectively zero coverage for recent deaths. Registry rows matched to a tweet_volume by death year: 2015 10/1097, 2016 42/1063, 2017 16/1075, 2018 14/1113, 2019 29/1085, 2020 33/1118, 2021 0/1101, 2022 0/1135, 2023 0/1173, 2024 1/1188. From 2021-01-06 onward every candidate in every episode scores p = 0. Because victim_registry.csv is strictly date-descending (verified is_monotonic_decreasing == True) and pandas' sort_values is stable, the tie at zero resolves to file order, so candidate_events silently changes meaning from "the two most prominent victims near the episode" to "the two most recent deaths at or before the episode end". 31 of 40 extension episodes and 8 of 30 discovery episodes have no prominence signal at all. Episode 52 (2021-04-06 to 2021-04-28, peak 3.12, Wright + Chauvin verdict) settles the causal question: Daunte Wright died 2021-04-11 and IS inside the existing 14-day window, yet he is not surfaced because he has no tweet_volume; the label is "Oscar Herrera; Dalton James Gerrit Kooiman", two 2021-04-28 deaths. Widening the window without replacing the ranking key would change nothing for any episode after 2020.

ADDITIONAL DEFECT, same error class, found while verifying: ranking joins on lowercased name strings, so a name collision transfers a famous victim's prominence to an unrelated person. The registry contains four Michael Browns (2014-08-09 Ferguson MO; 2016-01-31 Fort Worth TX; 2017-06-15 Newton NH; 2024-06-05 Milford CT) and the prominence table has a single "Michael Brown" with tweet_volume 10037. Episode 22 (2017-06-17 to 2017-06-23, DISCOVERY period, peak 2.33) is therefore labelled "Michael Brown; Charleena Lyles": the New Hampshire Michael Brown inherits Ferguson's volume and outranks Charleena Lyles, the Seattle case that actually drove the spike. This contaminates the discovery-period labels too, not just the extension.

CORRECTED FIX: replace the ranking key before touching the window. Rank candidates by post-episode Wikipedia pageviews (already available in data/reference/wikipedia_pageviews_victims.csv, 45 articles) or another measure defined over the whole 2015-2024 range, join on a stable victim id rather than a name string, and only then widen the lookback (60+ days) so video-release- and verdict-driven spikes can attach to the right death. Independently, audit the registry for omissions (Prude) and state that an MPV-derived registry structurally cannot capture non-police killings such as Neely.

title: The 129-day mega-episode discards 114 of its own days and hides at least eight separate attention events, including the two most on-hypothesis ones
fix: Adopt a rule that can resolve multiple events inside a sustained high period (peak/prominence detection, or hysteresis with a separate exit threshold), and cap episode length so no "event" exceeds the event window it is analysed with. Report how many above-threshold days enter the estimation sample under the chosen rule — that number should not be 43%.
claim: Episode 45 runs 2020-05-26 to 2020-10-01 (129 calendar days inclusive; docs/DATA_AUDIT.md:137 says 128). Under EVENT_WINDOW_PRE/POST = 14 (scripts/config.py:120-121) the design uses only 2020-05-12..2020-06-09 of it. The remaining 114 days are in no window at all: not treated, not control, simply absent. Within those discarded days sit distinct attention shocks that the merge rule refuses to call events.
corrected_claim: Episode 45 (data/reference/confirmation_episodes.csv:46) runs 2020-05-26 to 2020-10-01: 129 days inclusive (docs/DATA_AUDIT.md:137 reports 128, the date difference), 113 of them above the cai_d > 1.0 threshold (scripts/config.py:96). Because scripts/event_study.py:15-40 anchors each event window on the episode START and never on its length, EVENT_WINDOW_PRE/POST = 14 (scripts/config.py:120-121) means the design uses only 2020-05-12..2020-06-09 — 15 of the episode's own 129 days. Of the remaining 114: 112 are in no window at all, and 2 (2020-09-30 and 2020-10-01, both above threshold) enter as rel_day -14/-13 CONTROL days for episode 46, i.e. above-threshold days serving as the baseline for a later event. Inside the discarded stretch, find_peaks on cai_d (height > 1.0, prominence >= 0.5, min separation 7d) resolves 8 distinct local peaks — 2020-05-31 (5.36), 06-24 (4.12), 07-26 (1.84), 08-05 (1.93), 08-12 (1.47), 08-27 (2.72), 09-03 (2.60), 09-24 (2.17). cai_d reaches 1.91 on 2020-08-24 (Jacob Blake) and 2.05/2.44 on 2020-09-02 / 09-04 (release of the Daniel Prude body-camera footage); those values exceed the peak of 54 of the 70 frozen episodes and 22 of the 30 discovery episodes, not 20 of 70 as originally stated. Across the discovery window, 210 days clear the threshold; 90 (42.9%) reach a surviving post window, 98 (46.7%) fall in no window at all, and 15 more are dropped as duplicates. Episode 45 holds 53.8% of above-threshold days (113/210) and 68.2% of summed above-threshold cai_d, and enters the stacked design as a single 14-day event. Daniel Prude is absent from data/reference/victim_registry.csv — there is no Rochester, NY 2020 record at all, and the registry does carry Physical Restraint deaths, so this is a real gap; separately, scripts/13_extension_episodes.py:40 matches victims by DEATH date in [start-14, end], so even a repaired registry could not attach Prude (died 2020-03-30) to the September attention spike. Jacob Blake's absence is NOT a defect: he survived, and the registry is a killed-by-police list. The proposed fix (multi-event resolution inside sustained high periods, an episode-length cap tied to the analysis window, and a reported share of above-threshold days entering the estimation sample) is the right remedy.

title: Nine of 30 discovery episodes never contribute the reference day, and five contribute only post-treatment days whose effect the fixed effect absorbs
fix: Truncate the pre-window at the previous episode's end (lo = max(s-pre, prev_end+1)) instead of letting it collide and be deleted, and drop any episode that cannot retain rel_day -1 and at least one post day rather than stacking a degenerate window. Report per-rel_day episode counts alongside the event-time path so unbalanced composition is visible.
claim: `build_stack` truncates each window at the next episode's start (scripts/event_study.py:25-27) but does not truncate the *pre* window at the previous episode's end, then drops all copies of any district-day claimed twice (lines 38-39). When two episodes are within 14 days, the second episode's entire pre-window is destroyed. The result is that many stacked episodes have no day -1, and five have no pre-period at all — for those, the `ep_cd` fixed effect absorbs exactly the level shift the design is trying to measure, so their contribution to the day 0..7 statistic is a within-post contrast (or, when the surviving window is exactly days 0..7, algebraically zero net of noise).
corrected_claim: All factual and numeric content of the finding reproduces exactly against scripts/event_study.py and data/reference/confirmation_episodes.csv: 118 of 722 claimed calendar days (16.3%) are claimed by more than one window and every copy is deleted by the keep=False dedup (event_study.py:38-39), because the window's lower bound is never truncated at the previous episode (only hi is truncated, event_study.py:25-27); 21 of 30 episodes retain rel_day -1; episodes 2, 7, 10, 13, 29 have no surviving pre days and episodes 1, 6, 9, 12, 28 no surviving post days; episode 13 survives as exactly rel_days 0..7 and episode 29 (2020-10-21, Walter Wallace Jr.) as 0..14 with no pre period; only 9 of 30 keep the full -14..+14 window; 33 of 189 first-week cells (17.5%) come from no-pre episodes; and days 0..7 are identified off 22-25 different episodes while day -1 rests on 21. The FE-absorption mechanism is confirmed by simulation on the real stack geometry: an effect placed only in the five no-pre episodes (equal-weight truth 0.167) is recovered as +0.023, and tau=5.0 in episode 13 alone is recovered as -0.014 against noise sd 0.051 — the ep_cd fixed effect does absorb exactly the level shift. The one clause to correct is the stated consequence: the five post-only episodes do NOT mechanically dilute the estimate toward zero — with a homogeneous effect the estimator remains unbiased with them included (truth 1.0 -> +1.008 with, +1.007 without). What actually breaks is that the estimand silently becomes the average over the 25 episodes that retain a pre-period rather than the 30 frozen episodes (effect only in the 25 pre-having episodes, equal-weight truth over 30 = 0.833, is recovered as +0.964), so attenuation follows only if the response is larger in the dropped five — which is a live risk precisely because Walter Wallace Jr. is one of them. Two verified additions: the panel filter total_calls>=5 never binds (0 of 7,552 CD-days below 5 on the available EMS page; all 59 districts present every day), so this is pure window arithmetic and not a data artifact; and separately, placebo_starts breaks its loop once a drawn start exceeds `latest`, so randomization draws average 15.8 episodes against the observed stack's 30, meaning the null is not composition-matched to the observed statistic either.

title: candidate_events labelling is entirely derived from the retired Twitter measure, and 39 of 70 labels are file-order artifacts
fix: Rebuild prominence from a source that spans 2015-2024 and is keyed on identity, not name — per-victim Wikipedia pageviews in the 0-14 days after the episode peak, joined on the resolved article title rather than lowercase name. Retract the "labels are correct" line in docs/DATA_AUDIT.md:159-165 and re-run the check as "is the named person the highest-attention victim in the window", not "is the date in range". Where no candidate clears a prominence floor, write an empty label rather than a file-order default.
claim: scripts/13_extension_episodes.py:35 builds the prominence map from `tweet_volume` in data/reference/wikipedia_article_resolution.csv — the retired Twitter series (scripts/config.py:19-25 declares it "never a treatment in a reported result"). Only 150 names have any volume, so for most episodes every candidate ties at 0 and `sort_values("p", ascending=False)` (line 41) is a stable sort that returns the registry's own file order. corrected_claim: candidate_events labelling in scripts/13_extension_episodes.py:34-41 ranks candidates by `tweet_volume`, i.e. the retired Twitter per-victim measure (built at scripts/09_fetch_public_data.py:146-148,182 from TWEETS_PER_VICTIM_CSV, declared legacy-only at scripts/config.py:20-25). Only the top-150 names by tweet volume carry any value (WIKI_TOP_N = 150, scripts/09_fetch_public_data.py:83), so 150 of 13,241 registry rows (1.13%) are rankable. In 39 of 70 episodes every candidate ties at 0.0, and the stable `sort_values("p", ascending=False)` at line 41 returns the registry's own date-descending file order: I asserted for all 39 that the label equals the first two rows of the window, and that the first name is the latest death in the window. Candidate pool median 48, max 400 (episode 45). Coverage of tweet_volume ends at death year 2020, so every episode starting 2021 or later is a file-order artifact — 2021 4/4, 2022 12/12, 2023 5/5, 2024 1/1, i.e. 22 of the 39 (the original claim said 2022 on; it is one year worse). The remaining 17 are 2015-2019. Separately, the prominence map is keyed on lowercase name (line 35), so all four "Michael Brown" registry rows (2014-08-09 Ferguson MO, 2016-01-31 Fort Worth TX, 2017-06-15 Newton NH, 2024-06-05 Milford CT) inherit Ferguson's 10,037 tweets; episode 22 (discovery, 2017-06-17) is therefore labelled with the Newton NH Michael Brown and demotes Charleena Lyles (Seattle, mental-health crisis, 4,986) to second. The same logic is duplicated at scripts/12_build_cai.py:136-143 and writes the committed table outputs/tables/cai_top_days.csv. docs/DATA_AUDIT.md:159-163 ("0 of 140 labels are out of window ... No relabelling is needed") and outputs/tables/data_audit.csv line 32 rest on scripts/20_data_audit.py:171-185, which tests only whether the named person's death date falls in a 21-day-pre window — looser even than the 14-day window the generator uses — and so cannot detect either failure mode. Two evidentiary corrections to the original finding: the prominence input is the per-victim file 211118_tweet_count_name_date.csv, not the daily 220126_final_daily_tweet_count.csv, and neither Twitter raw file is present in the working tree or git index, so the "file ends 2022-01-26" reasoning is unverifiable — the 2020 coverage cutoff is established empirically instead. No estimate changes: downstream consumers (scripts/07, 08, 17, 18) read only start/end dates from this file.

title: placebo_starts builds a null from half-size, calendar-skewed designs; the ratified primary p-value has near-zero size
fix: Replace the anchor-and-walk with a draw that preserves BOTH the episode count and every gap: circularly shift the whole vector of real start dates by a uniform offset, wrapping inside [lo+pre+1, hi-post-1]. (Rejection-sampling anchors until all 30 fit also works but wastes ~92% of draws and still tilts early.) Separately, use the (1+#{|b_perm|>=|b_obs|})/(1+B) form of the p-value at event_study.py:143 and 04_robustness.py:82, and record how many draws were discarded rather than shrinking the denominator silently.
claim: event_study.py:100-122 draws ONE uniform anchor and then walks forward with permuted gaps, breaking when the walk runs past the window end. The real 30 discovery episodes span sum(gaps)=1324 days inside an eligible window of only 1431 days, so the walk almost always truncates. The placebo designs are therefore systematically smaller and later than the observed design, are not exchangeable with it, and produce a null distribution that is far too wide.
corrected_claim: placebo_starts (scripts/event_study.py:115-121) draws one uniform anchor and walks forward through permuted gaps, breaking at the first gap that overshoots the window end. The 30 discovery episodes span sum(gaps)=1324 days inside an eligible window of 1430 days, so only 7.8% of anchors admit all 30; draws average 16.1 episodes and 19,497 stack rows against the observed 30 and 35,636 (55%), and are calendar-skewed late (41.9% of placebo starts fall in 2020 vs 20.0% of real starts). Placebo assignments are therefore not exchangeable with the observed assignment and the null is far too wide: on 18_null_calibration.py's own generator the placebo statistics have SD 0.00234 against the observed statistic's sampling SD of 0.00114 — a ratio of 2.05, worse than the 1.64 originally reported. Running randomization_p end to end on 26 pure-noise panels gives 0/26 rejections at both alpha=0.05 and alpha=0.10, median p = 0.758, min p = 0.244; P(all 26 uniform p-values exceed 0.244) = 0.0007. The size at nominal 5% is effectively zero. CORRECTION TO THE ORIGINAL FINDING: the test is not powerless — a citywide days-0..7 shock of -0.005 (0.17 SD) is rejected 69% of the time at alpha=0.05 (median p = 0.038). The distortion is one-directional and conservative, so a rejection remains trustworthy; what is destroyed is the evidential content of a NON-rejection, which is the modal outcome and which GATE_C_MEMO.md:139-141/:252-259 designates the primary confirmatory p-value. ESCALATION: the synthetic-null calibration that Gate C makes a hard precondition has ALREADY RUN and already recorded the symptom — outputs/tables/null_calibration.csv carries empirical_rejection_rate = 0.0 and median_p = 0.7142 — yet stamps VERDICT: CALIBRATED, because 18_null_calibration.py:129-131 sets the acceptance band to alpha +/- 1.96*sqrt(alpha(1-alpha)/n), which at n=12 sims is [-0.0733, 0.1733] and so contains zero. The band widens as evidence thins, and it tests only whether the point estimate sits near alpha rather than whether the p-values are uniform. Both defects must be fixed together: replacing the draw mechanism alone would leave a guard that cannot detect a recurrence, and fixing the guard alone would merely convert a false PASS into a block. Fix the draw with a circular shift of the whole start vector inside [lo+pre+1, hi-post-1] (verified: 30 episodes every draw, mean stack 35,778 rows, ratio 1.004 to observed); replace the calibration verdict with a uniformity test (e.g. KS on the p-values) at a sim count that can actually resolve 5%; use the (1+#{|b_perm|>=|b_obs|})/(1+B) p-value at event_study.py:143 and 04_robustness.py:82; and record discarded draws rather than shrinking the denominator silently, as outputs/tables/null_calibration_pvalues.csv shows it currently does (denominators 23, 24, 25 against draws=25).

title: The omitted event-time category is day -14, not day -1, and the 1,239 day -1 observations are deleted from the fit
fix: Keep the rel_day==-1 rows in the sample and set the reference explicitly, e.g. pf.feols(f"{outcome} ~ i(rel_day, ref={EVENT_REFERENCE_DAY}) | {fe}") or C(rel_day, Treatment(reference=-1)), then assert that the returned coefficient set omits exactly EVENT_REFERENCE_DAY. Consider a pooled pre-period baseline (mean of -14..-2) instead of any single day, which cuts the base-cell variance contribution by ~13x.
claim: event_study.py:59 removes rows with rel_day == EVENT_REFERENCE_DAY from the estimation sample instead of making that level the omitted base. formulaic's C() then takes the smallest surviving level, -14, as the reference. Every reported coefficient and the H1 statistic are normalized to day -14, and the day -1 data is thrown away.
corrected_claim: Confirmed as stated, with two refinements. (1) The cited observation counts (1,239 at rel_day=-1, 1,003 at -14, 1,475 at day 0) are exact for a fully balanced 59-district design grid and reproduce precisely, but they cannot come from the real EMS panel, which is not present in this repo (data/processed/panel_cd_day.parquet is absent and data/processed/ems_pages ends 2016-06-10). They are pre-filter counts; 17_stacked_event_study.py:82's total_calls>=5 filter would reduce them on real data. The defect itself is unaffected: the omitted level is -14, 27 coefficients are returned for -13..-2 and 0..+14, and the rel_day==-1 rows are deleted from the estimation sample, all determined by the episode dates and window logic alone. (2) The -14 base cell is the sparsest, tied with +14 at 1,003 obs from 17 of 30 episodes. Two additions: the deleted -1 rows also stop contributing to the ep_cd and dow fixed effects, not just the event-time dummies; and event_study_path.csv omits both -1 and -14, so the base day is absent rather than plotted at zero. The docstring contradiction extends to docs/REWORK_PLAN.md:204 as well as config.py:123 and 17_stacked_event_study.py:13-15. The existing null calibration (outputs/tables/null_calibration.csv) is not invalidated by this, since rejection rates under the null do not depend on the choice of base day.

title: first_week_effect is a single linear contrast, not the pre-registered joint test, and has exactly zero power against the deferral pattern the project itself predicts
fix: Pre-specify one of two things and implement it: (a) a joint Wald/F on the eight day-0..7 coefficients (matching 03_main_model.py's eigenvalue-truncated wald(), which already handles the near-singular V), with the mean reported as the directional summary; or (b) keep the mean but state in CONFIRMATION_PLAN/GATE_C that H1 is a test of the AVERAGE first-week level, not a joint test, and add the dip-vs-rebound contrast as a named secondary. Separately, either wire counts=True into 17 with a real log(total_calls) offset/regressor or delete the claim from the docstring.
claim: config.H1_TEST = 'two_sided_joint_lags_0_7' and GATE_C_MEMO.md §6.1 ratify a 'two-sided joint test' of lags 0-7. event_study.py:78-97 implements the unweighted MEAN of the eight day-0..7 coefficients. A mean is one 1-df contrast: it is the most powerful statistic against a flat sustained shift and has literally no power against any mean-zero rearrangement within the week.
corrected_claim: Substantively correct as written; three precision fixes. (1) "Exactly zero power" should be "power equal to size": under randomization inference a mean-zero-within-week effect yields a statistic distributed as under the null, so rejection stays at alpha — my run gives p_RI=0.737 for a strong deferral effect against p_RI=0.633 for the pure null, i.e. practically zero power, not literally zero. (2) The Uvalde-shaped first_week_effect reproduces as about -0.0031 (my RNG stream), not -0.00252; the arithmetic mean of the injected path is -0.002625, so the attenuation versus the -0.008 peak is roughly 2.5-3x rather than strictly "less than a third". (3) The genuine joint Wald is the `wald()` function at 03_main_model.py:136-159 (166-170 is the test_sets dict), and the same 8-df test also exists as `joint07` at 03c_cai_discovery_robustness.py:51-64 — which is where GATE_C_MEMO §1's and §6.0's quoted "joint lags 0-7" p-values (0.041 / 0.006) actually come from, so the ratified phrase "joint test" provably refers to an 8-df Wald and not to a mean. One addition strengthening the counts half: 17 passes H1_OUTCOMES = ("edp_share","mh_narrow_share"), so even if counts=True were wired in, the dormant fepois path would be handed SHARE outcomes — it lacks a count outcome as well as an offset.

title: 18_null_calibration's PASS verdict cannot fail, and the committed artifact was produced at 12 sims / 25 draws with no real panel
fix: Refuse to emit a verdict below a minimum n_sims (200) and n_draws (>=500). Build the interval around the OBSERVED rate (Clopper-Pearson on rej) and fail when it excludes alpha in EITHER direction — under-rejection is a failure, not a pass. Add an explicit uniformity test on the p-values (KS vs U(0,1)) as a second, independently reported criterion. Refuse to run at all when panel_cd_day.parquet is absent, rather than silently falling back to assumed parameters and stamping a verdict.
claim: The gate that Gate C §6.3 makes a precondition for the confirmatory run is not capable of blocking it. The acceptance band at 18:129-131 is alpha ± 1.96*sqrt(alpha(1-alpha)/n_sims) — centred on alpha and computed from ALPHA's variance rather than the estimate's — so at small n_sims it accepts a rejection rate of zero, and the script has no minimum-n guard. The second failure mode the docstring names ('p-values piled at 0 or 1 rather than uniform') is never tested: median_p is written to the CSV at 18:141 and never enters the verdict at 18:131.
corrected_claim:
Substantially confirmed, with three corrections.

CONFIRMED (reproduced exactly). Replicating 18_null_calibration.py's code path with its hardcoded seed 18:58 (rng = default_rng(18_20260908)) at 12 sims / 25 draws returns values identical to outputs/tables/null_calibration.csv down to the last digit of mean_null_effect (1.0273375635871986e-05), median_p 0.7142, rej 0.0, band [-0.0733, 0.1733], VERDICT CALIBRATED. data/processed/panel_cd_day.parquet does not exist, so the calibration branch at 18:69-81 never fired and the run used the assumed rho=0.6/sigma=0.03/mu=0.10 at 18:67 while documented defaults are 200/200 (18:51-52, docstring 18:30). The band at 18:129-131 has no minimum-n guard, and median_p (written 18:141) never enters `calibrated` at 18:131, so the docstring's second failure mode (18:27, non-uniform p-values) is never tested. Gate C §6.3 (docs/GATE_C_MEMO.md:252-259) does make this a precondition in those words. Independently strengthened: a 40-sim run at a different seed gives rej=0.000, median_p=0.68, minimum p across 40 sims = 0.12 — the under-rejection is a real property of the estimator, not sampling noise — and the verdict was still CALIBRATED. Exact threshold: `lo` stays <= 0 for all n_sims <= 72, so a rejection rate of zero cannot produce a FAIL below n_sims = 73.

CORRECTION 1 — the artifact is NOT committed. .gitignore:50 ignores outputs/tables/*.csv; `git ls-files outputs/` returns only two .gitkeep files. null_calibration.csv is an untracked working-tree file, which weakens "anyone reading null_calibration.csv would conclude the precondition is closed" to a local rather than a repo-published claim.

CORRECTION 2 — "cannot fail" is literally too strong. At n=12 the upper edge is 0.1733, so 3/12 = 0.25 would emit NOT CALIBRATED. Accurate: it cannot fail in the UNDER-rejection direction below n_sims=73, and at n=12 tolerates up to 2/12 = 16.7% over-rejection.

CORRECTION 3 — the diagnosis mislocates the bug, and the proposed fix follows from that mislocation. Centring on alpha and using the null variance alpha(1-alpha) is the standard, correct construction for testing H0: rate = alpha; it is not the defect, and Clopper-Pearson on the observed rate is not an improvement for this purpose. The defect is (a) the normal approximation is void at n=12, where expected rejections = 0.6, and (b) the absence of a minimum-n guard. No choice of interval rescues n=12: even an exact binomial test cannot flag it, since P(0 rejections in 12 | true rate 0.05) = 0.540. Similarly, "fail in EITHER direction — under-rejection is a failure, not a pass" is already the code's intent (18:131 is two-sided; 18:156 prints an "UNDER" direction); it failed to fire because of n, not because under-rejection was exempted. The surviving parts of the fix are: a minimum n_sims (>=200) and n_draws floor, refusing to emit a verdict or to run at all when panel_cd_day.parquet is absent, and adding an explicit uniformity test (KS vs U(0,1)) as a second reported criterion.

title: build_stack's de-duplication deletes 28% of window district-days and removes the entire first week of 5 of the 30 episodes
fix: Resolve collisions by assignment rather than deletion: give each district-day to exactly one event (nearest start, or first claim), so no episode loses its whole treated week. Then emit the per-rel_day episode count and per-episode first-week-day count next to event_study_path.csv, and assert that every episode contributes at least min_days of the 0..7 window before it enters the statistic.
claim: The truncation rule at event_study.py:27 fixes forward overlap only; the NEXT episode's pre-window still collides with the current episode's post-window, and the fix at event_study.py:38-39 deletes the collision from BOTH events. With clustered episodes this removes the treated week of the earlier event, so the H1 statistic is computed on an unequally weighted subset of episodes and each rel_day coefficient is estimated on a different set of episodes.
corrected_claim:
CONFIRMED AS STATED on all factual content. `build_stack` truncates windows forward only (event_study.py:27) while the next episode's pre-window still opens inside the current episode's post-window, and `duplicated(..., keep=False)` at event_study.py:38-39 deletes the collision from BOTH episodes. On the real 30 discovery episodes with pre=post=14 this drops 13,924 of 49,560 window district-days (28.1%; 40.1% at post=28, 43.8% at post=60). Episodes 1, 6, 9, 12 and 28 contribute ZERO day-0..7 observations; episode 2 contributes 2 days, 18 contributes 4, 7 contributes 7. Per-rel_day episode composition runs 17 (at -14) to 25 (at day 0), so no two coefficients on the exported path average over the same events. Dropped days carry 24% higher CAI-D than kept days (0.408 vs 0.330, n=236 vs 604, Welch t=1.38, p=0.17). MIN_FIRST_WEEK_DAYS=6 does not catch this because it counts pooled identified coefficients, not per-episode contribution.

Two corrections to the interpretation:

(1) The bias direction is the OPPOSITE of what the finding claims. The 5 episodes losing their whole treated week are the LOW-intensity ones (mean peak_cai_d 1.33 vs 1.65 for the other 25). All five highest-intensity episodes keep a full 8-day first week, including George Floyd (2020-05-26, peak 5.36). The statistic rests on 25 of 30 episodes, but it retains the strongest spikes and discards weak, tightly-spaced ones — so the composition problem is real but the effect is likely to inflate the apparent first-week response, not attenuate it.

(2) The placebo drop-rate argument does not hold. `placebo_starts` permutes the same gap multiset, and pairwise overlap length is a function of gap alone (29-g for g<=14, else 14), so deletion is near permutation-invariant: over 200 draws the placebo drop rate is mean 0.251 / median 0.272 against 0.281 observed. The genuine observed-vs-placebo mismatch is elsewhere and larger — `placebo_starts` breaks the chain at event_study.py:119-120 when a draw exceeds `latest`, so placebo stacks carry a median of 16 episodes and ~26,100 raw rows against the observed 30 and 49,560. That is a separate defect and should be filed separately.

One addition that strengthens the finding: the base cell is rel_day -14, not -1. event_study.py:59 DELETES rel_day == -1 from the estimation sample instead of setting it as the omitted category, so `C(rel_day)` falls back to the minimum surviving level. The docstring at 17_stacked_event_study.py:13-15 ("Day EVENT_REFERENCE_DAY (-1) is the omitted category, so every coefficient reads as the change relative to the day before attention rose") is therefore false, and the reference cell every coefficient is differenced against is built from only 17 of the 30 episodes.

The proposed fix (assign each district-day to exactly one event, then export per-rel_day episode counts and assert a per-episode first-week minimum) is correct and should be adopted, with the reference-day bug fixed at the same time.

title: Both the null generator and the reported SEs ignore citywide day shocks — REWORK_PLAN I1, relearned in the new code
fix: Use vcov={'CRV1': 'date_id'} (or cluster by episode, whichever is more conservative) in fit_event_study and at 17:111, and report which was used in the output. Add a citywide AR(1) component to synthetic_panel() and calibrate its variance from the real panel's day-level residual variance (var of the cross-district daily mean after CD and dow FE) rather than from a per-district AR(1) — which means 18 genuinely cannot run before the panel exists. Stop reporting null_sd as a standard error.
claim: Treatment is citywide: on a given calendar date all 59 districts share the same rel_day, so the DAY is the unit of assignment and the effective sample is ~1,461 days, not 35,636 district-days. REWORK_PLAN.md:17 (defect I1) says exactly this and mandates date clustering as primary inference. The new estimator does neither: event_study.py:66 and 17_stacked_event_study.py:111 use vcov='hetero', and 18's synthetic panel (18:95-109) draws independent per-district AR(1) with no common day component at all.
corrected_claim:
The vcov half is correct. Treatment is assigned at the date level -- build_stack (event_study.py:33) sets rel_day from the calendar date and dedups overlapping windows (:38-39), so all 59 districts on a date share one rel_day; the stack is 35,636 rows over 583 dates and 30 episodes. event_study.py:65-66 and 17_stacked_event_study.py:111 nonetheless fit with vcov='hetero', against REWORK_PLAN.md:17 (I1), which mandates date clustering as primary, and against 03_main_model.py:84, which already does it.

Simulated on 18's own fallback DGP (59x1461, rho=0.6, sigma=0.03, the 30 discovery starts): with no citywide component the hetero SE is already right -- true sampling SD of the day+3 coefficient 0.001226 vs mean SE 0.001211, ratio 1.01 (a second run: 0.001139 vs 0.001210, ratio 0.94). So the finding's claimed 1.11x penalty from within-district AR(1) alone is Monte Carlo noise, not a real effect: episodes are weeks apart, so a daily AR(1) barely correlates the cells that identify a rel_day coefficient. Add a citywide AR(1) day shock of sd 0.010 and the true sampling SD rises to 0.00373 / 0.00336 while the hetero SE moves only to 0.00127 -- a 2.6-2.9x understatement across two runs, close to the claimed 3.14x. The first-week statistic's SD rises 2.95x (0.00106 -> 0.00313). CRV1 on date_id (583 clusters) restores correct coverage (ratio 1.03 with the shock, 0.98 without); CRV1 on episode (30 clusters) is slightly conservative (0.95 / 0.89). So the fix -- vcov={'CRV1':'date_id'} in fit_event_study and at 17:111, with the choice reported in the output -- is right, and must be made before event_study_path.csv feeds PAPER_PLAN's main-text Figure 2 (section 4, line 204 -- NOT section 6.2, which is a STROBE row on call-code validation). Reporting null_sd (17:125) as a dispersion measure is separately wrong.

The 18 half is refuted. 18 does not calibrate a variance; it calibrates a randomization-inference p-value (18:115, verdict at 18:143), and RI is scale-free because the observed and placebo statistics come from the same synthetic panel and inherit the same citywide component. Measured at 120 sims x 100 draws per condition, adding the missing day shock changes nothing: rejection rate 0.000 vs 0.000 at alpha=0.05, 0.00833 vs 0.00833 at alpha=0.10, median p 0.655 vs 0.679. The absence of a common day component in synthetic_panel() therefore does not invalidate 18's verdict, and 18 does not need the real panel for this reason.

Consequently the defect does not block the confirmatory run -- the primary p-value is RI and is unaffected -- it corrupts only the reported standard errors and the main-text figure's error bars. Two further corrections: the effective unit count for this estimator is 583 dates / 30 episodes, not the ~1,461 quoted from I1 (which describes the distributed-lag model); and since panel_cd_day.parquet does not exist and outputs/tables holds no event_study_path.csv, 17 has never run, so this is a latent code defect rather than a wrong number already in an output.

claim: 07_did_exposure.py:69-78 stacks +/-7-day windows with next-start truncation but performs no de-duplication. Truncation removes forward overlap only, so the pre-window of episode i+1 still overlaps the post-window of episode i, and the same district-day enters the regression twice — once as treated and once as control.
corrected_claim:
07_did_exposure.py:70-78 stacks +/-7-day episode windows with forward-only truncation (line 73) and never de-duplicates, so the pre-window of episode i+1 overlaps the post-window of episode i. Replaying it on the 30 discovery starts: 418 window-days per district after dropping rel_day 0, of which 52 rows (26 dates x 2) are duplicates — 12.4% of the sample, 3,068 CD-day rows in `win`.
