title: Randomization inference draws placebo designs with about half the real number of episodes, inflating the null SD 2x and roughly doubling the primary p-value
fix: Make every draw carry exactly len(real_starts) episodes: wrap the gap chain circularly within the window (modulo the window length), or reject-and-redraw anchors that would truncate. Then also block the draw on season - draw placebo chains that reproduce the real episodes' month distribution (or add calendar-month fixed effects to the stacked regression) so the null is exchangeable with respect to season. Re-run 18_null_calibration.py after the fix and require the rejection rate to sit inside the band from BOTH sides, reporting the null SD alongside the rejection rate.
claim: scripts/event_study.py:100-122 `placebo_starts` picks an anchor uniformly on the whole admissible range and then walks forward through a permutation of the real gaps, breaking (line 120-121) as soon as a date exceeds `latest`. Because the real episode chain spans almost the whole window, nearly every anchor truncates the chain. The placebo designs therefore have fewer events than the real design, their first-week statistics are much noisier, and the null distribution used at line 143 is far too wide. This violates the basic requirement of placebo/randomization inference (Canay-Romano-Shaikh; MacKinnon & Webb; Ferman & Pinto) that the placebo assignments be drawn from the same distribution as the real assignment.
corrected_claim:
CONFIRMED with two quantitative corrections. `scripts/event_study.py:115-121` (`placebo_starts`) draws an anchor uniformly on the full admissible range and walks forward through a permutation of the real gaps, breaking as soon as a date exceeds `latest`. Because the permuted gaps always sum to the real chain's span (1,324 days) while the admissible anchor range is 1,430 days, the full chain survives only for anchors in the first 106 days. Reproduced with the project's own function: 30 discovery episodes over 2017-01-01..2020-12-31, 2,000 draws -> placebo episode count mean 16.21, median 16, 5th-95th [2, 30]; 92.0% of draws carry fewer than 30 episodes and 15.0% carry <=5. Full 70-episode list over 2015-2024: median 37 vs 70 real, 94.7% short. The observed statistic (`event_study.py:128`) is built from ALL real starts, so observed and null come from different designs. Nothing screens the short draws out: `event_study.py:136` requires only len(ps)>=2, and MIN_FIRST_WEEK_DAYS does not bind because short chains have longer gaps and therefore LESS window truncation.

CORRECTION 1 (magnitude). On a synthetic null panel built exactly as `scripts/18_null_calibration.py:97-110` does it (59 CDs, rho=0.6, sigma=0.03), the placebo SD as coded is 0.00205 against 0.00112 when every draw is forced to carry all 30 episodes -- a factor of 1.83x, not the claimed 2.0x. Dispersion by placebo count reproduces: <=5 eps SD 0.00367, 6-10 0.00228, 11-20 0.00162, 21-30 0.00120. Because the coded null is a heavy-tailed mixture over episode counts rather than a single normal, a statistic sitting at the correct null's two-sided 5% threshold (0.00220) reports p ~= 0.22 under the coded null, not the claimed ~0.33. The conclusion is unchanged: a genuinely p=0.05 result is reported as a clear null, a ~4x inflation.

CORRECTION 2 (seasonality). The month mismatch is real (May 23.3% and February 0% of real discovery starts) but its consequence is overstated. `fit_event_study` uses `ep_cd + dow` fixed effects (`event_study.py:38`, :62-66), so seasonal LEVEL differences are absorbed within each +/-14-day window; only within-28-day seasonal shape can contaminate the estimate. Also, the placebo months are not the uniform ~8%/month claimed -- the forward walk tilts them monotonically (Jan 6.6% to Nov 9.8%), a second unremarked calendar artefact of the same construction.

ADDITIONAL CORROBORATION not in the original finding: the committed `outputs/tables/null_calibration.csv` already records `median_p = 0.7142` (should be ~0.5 under a calibrated randomization test on no-effect data) -- direct in-repo evidence of the conservatism. That run has `n_sims_completed = 12`, which makes `acceptable_range_lo = -0.0733` (`18_null_calibration.py:128-130`), so its `rejection_rate = 0.0` could not possibly have failed; it was stamped `VERDICT,CALIBRATED`.

title: trends_victims is a within-window rank normalisation: every victim, from Walter Scott to George Floyd, peaks at exactly 100, so the component carries no information about relative event magnitude
fix: Drop trends_victims from CAI-D (which DATA_AUDIT §2 already recommends) and fix the docstring. If a victim-name component is wanted, re-fetch each victim window against a benchmark term with stable, high volume that exceeds every victim name in every window (Hölzl et al. §4.2(2); DiGrazia 2015), and divide by the benchmark column so the units are genuinely common - or use the Wu et al. relative-frequency approach the project already cites in RELATED_WORK §1D.
claim: scripts/11c_trends_anchor_and_victims.py:88-98 fetches one Google Trends payload per victim over event-30d..event+120d with the pair [victim name, "police brutality"], then at line 95 takes `ratio = df[name].astype(float)` - the raw victim column, never divided by the topic column - and sums it across victims (line 97-98). Each payload is normalised 0-100 within its own window, so whichever term is the window maximum gets 100. The docstring at :8-11 claims the values are "expressed in topic units and therefore comparable across victims"; the code does no such transformation. Hölzl et al. (2025) §4.2(2) state the condition explicitly: to put separately-retrieved Trends datasets on a common scale the shared benchmark term must be MORE popular than every term of interest in every window, so the maximum is always assigned to the benchmark. "Police brutality" is not - it is dwarfed by the victim name in every major window.
corrected_claim:
Confirmed as stated, with three small corrections and two additions.

CORRECTIONS. (a) Line numbers are off by one: the victim payload is fetched at scripts/11c_trends_anchor_and_victims.py:90, `ratio = df[name].astype(float)` is at :96 (not :95), the summation at :97-98, and the docstring comparability claim at :8-10 (not :8-11). (b) The topic column is not entirely unused in the victim loop — it is read at :91 as an inclusion filter (`df[TOPIC].max() == 0` -> skip the window). It is never used as a divisor, which is what the claim requires, and this filter is in fact the availability-endogeneity mechanism DATA_AUDIT §2 documents. (c) "Police brutality ... is dwarfed by the victim name in every major window" is directly verifiable only for the four non-overlapping windows; elsewhere the summed series cannot be decomposed into per-victim curves. This does not weaken the finding: Trends columns are 0-100 by construction, so with no division there is no common scale regardless of which term takes the window maximum.

STRENGTHENED. The finding's core mechanism can be proven directly rather than inferred. Four of the 18 curated windows overlap no other window, so on those dates the summed component equals that one victim's raw column: Stephon Clark (2018) 100.0, Laquan McDonald (2018) 100.0, Atatiana Jefferson (2019) 100.0, Daunte Wright (2021) 100.0. Four unrelated cases spanning four years, each peaking at exactly 100.0. And every peak above 100 sits on a multi-window day: Floyd 135 at k=4, Brooks 148 at k=4, Sterling/Castile 198 at k=2 — 99.0 per window, i.e. two names retrieved in near-identical windows each reaching ~100 and simply adding.

ADDED. Two further defects surfaced while verifying, both arguing for the same fix. First, scripts/12_build_cai.py:5 states CAI-D is "wiki_ext, trends_us, trends_nyc" while :36 sets D_COMPONENTS to include trends_victims — a third doc-vs-code contradiction, this one in the index build script itself, meaning a reader of that docstring would not know the component is in the index at all. Second, the per-component standardisation at :71-75 computes trends_victims' mean and SD over STD_WINDOW 2017-2019 from only 431 of 1,095 days, and those days are selected by the treatment-caused availability filter at 11c:91 — so the component's location and scale, not just its level, are set by an endogenously-selected subsample. This compounds the level-by-window-overlap problem rather than washing it out.

title: trends_nyc is Google's low-volume zero-censoring, at a censoring rate that rises from 55% to 98% of days, and its "anchoring" silently skips 42% of weeks
fix: Either drop trends_nyc from CAI-D and state in the Methods that no local-attention component was obtainable, or rebuild it with the Stephens-Davidowitz/DiGrazia benchmark-term method (fetch "police brutality + <stable high-volume benchmark>" and the benchmark alone, and difference) so the series clears the reporting floor. Whichever is chosen, report the per-year censoring rate in the validation battery, and make 11b/11c raise rather than silently substitute scale=1.0 when an overlap or period mean is zero.
claim: The NYC DMA series for the keyword "police brutality" is below Google's undisclosed privacy/low-volume reporting floor on most days, so it is returned as 0 (Hölzl et al. 2025 §4.2(1); Behnen et al. 2020; Mavragani & Ochoa 2019 all identify low-volume terms and small geographies as where Trends sample instability and zero-censoring bite hardest). After log1p and standardisation on 2017-2019 (scripts/12_build_cai.py:74-78) every censored day takes the identical constant -0.554, so in the later years the component is a near-constant that contributes no variance but shifts the CAI-D level. Separately, the anchoring loop at 11c:74-77 only rescales a period when the raw daily mean is strictly positive (`if m and m > 0`), so all-zero periods are silently left un-anchored.
corrected_claim:
trends_nyc ("police brutality", US-NY-501) is dominated by low-volume zero-censoring: it is exactly 0 on 2899 of 3653 days (79.4%), rising from 55-78% in 2015-2020 to 92.1%/92.1%/89.0%/98.4% in 2021-2024 (data/reference/cai_trends_anchored.csv). The censoring is a reporting floor, not rounding: the raw stitched NYC series has no nonzero value below 10.91 on the 0-100 chunk scale, while trends_us has 733 nonzero values below 5 (min 1.762); in 2024 only 6 days are nonzero and all sit at their 180-day chunk's maximum. After log1p and standardisation on 2017-2019 (scripts/12_build_cai.py:74-78) every censored day takes the identical constant -0.554082, and 98.6% of the reference-window variance of log1p(trends_nyc) is the binary zero/nonzero split rather than variation in magnitude (p0=0.7626, mean_nonzero=3.088, sd_nonzero=0.322). The reference SD (1.3234) is therefore essentially a function of the censoring rate, so standardised trends_nyc is not comparable between the 76.3%-censored discovery window and the 89-98%-censored confirmation window: its mean drifts from +0.025 (2017) to -0.501 (2024) with no attention content. docs/DATA_AUDIT.md:37-47 records trends_nyc availability as 1.00 in every year, so the project currently treats this component as fully present — the same exists-vs-means-the-same-thing error as wiki_ext and the component-count problem.

CORRECTIONS to the prior audit's supporting evidence. (a) The anchoring step is MONTHLY, not weekly: a 2015-2024 timeframe request returns monthly granularity, so `wk` at scripts/11c:73 holds ~120 points while the mask at :74 is 7 days wide, meaning only days 1-7 of each month are ever anchored (verified: all 178 rescaled trends_nyc days and all 834 rescaled trends_us days have day-of-month <= 7; 80%+ of days are never anchored at all). The `if m and m > 0` skip therefore drops 49 of 120 monthly anchor periods (40.8%), concentrated in the confirmation years — {2015:5, 2016:1, 2017:4, 2018:3, 2019:4, 2020:1, 2021:8, 2022:8, 2023:5, 2024:10} — not "222 of 523 weeks" with 38/33/32/46. (b) The 11b chunk-stitch no-op fired on 3 of 29 overlaps (2021-07-28..2021-09-25, 2022-07-23..2022-09-20, 2024-07-12..2024-09-09), not across a ~30-chunk chain; the other 26 overlaps were scaled by a positive ratio. (c) The component is not variance-free in the later years (standardised SD 0.632/0.838/1.014/0.415 for 2021-2024 vs ~1.0 in reference), and including it does not systematically shift the CAI-D level: mean cai_d with minus without trends_nyc is -0.136 (2021), -0.062 (2022), +0.027 (2023), +0.035 (2024), and corr(cai_d, cai_d ex-nyc) = 0.949. (d) Additional latent bug in the same line 11b:53: the guard covers only new_m == 0; if prev_m == 0 and new_m > 0 the scale evaluates to 0.0 and permanently zeroes the rest of the series (it did not fire in the current fetch).

The fix stands: drop trends_nyc or rebuild it with a benchmark-term difference so it clears the floor; report the per-year zero rate in the validation battery alongside the availability table; and make 11b/11c raise rather than silently substitute 1.0 (and never 0.0). The anchoring granularity bug at 11c:73-77 must be fixed independently of this finding.

title: The Google Trends "weekly anchor" is actually a MONTHLY series; only days 1-7 of each month were ever rescaled, leaving a 26% scale break inside every month
fix: Do not request >5-year windows for a weekly anchor. Fetch two overlapping <=5-year weekly series (e.g. 2015-01..2019-12 and 2019-01..2024-12) and splice them on the shared year, or implement the Caporin & Poli (2017) three-step procedure that Hölzl et al. §4.2(3) recommend (daily share within period -> weight by the period RSI -> renormalise). Assert that the returned index spacing is 7 days before using it, and add a day-of-month balance test (mean CAI-D and each component by day-of-month) to the validation battery in 12_build_cai.py. Because this changes CAI-D, the episode list must be regenerated under the DATA_AUDIT §6 procedure while outcomes are still blind.
claim: scripts/11c_trends_anchor_and_victims.py:61 requests a single Trends payload over "2015-01-01 2024-12-31". Google returns MONTHLY granularity for windows over 5 years (daily <= ~9 months, weekly <= 5 years) - documented in Hölzl, Keusch & Sajons (2025) SSR 126:103099 §1.2.2(3) and their Table 5 / §4.2(3). The code treats the returned index as weekly: line 74 builds the mask as `(index >= wstart) & (index < wstart + 7 days)`. With a monthly index, that mask covers only the first seven days of each month. Days 8-31 of every month are never rescaled and remain on the raw chain-stitched scale from 11b, whose 0-100 normalisation is a *daily*-window normalisation. The anchored series is therefore a mixture of two incompatible normalisations with a hard discontinuity at day 7->8 of every month, and the QC diagnostic that was printed (line 80-81, corr(stitched, anchored)) cannot detect it.
corrected_claim:
The mechanism, the code citations and every quoted number are correct. Three corrections:

(a) MISLABELLED, and the correction strengthens the finding. The table given as "Mean raw trends_us on days 1-7 vs days 8+ ... ratio 0.768/0.750/..." is not the raw series — it is the ANCHORED series (data/reference/cai_trends_anchored.csv). The d8+ column is common to both because those days are untouched, which is what disguised the slip. The genuinely RAW series (cai_trends_daily.csv) has d1-7/d8+ ratios of 0.98, 1.02, 1.02, 1.05, 0.97, 1.69, 0.99, 1.06, 0.98, 1.02 for 2015-2024 — i.e. no day-of-month gap at all outside 2020. So the ~26% level break is entirely MANUFACTURED by the anchoring step at :70-79; it is not a pre-existing feature that anchoring failed to fix. The 120 month scale factors applied to d1-7 have median 0.744, range 0.337 to 3.642, and 85% are below 1.

(b) SCOPE. "834 days" is trends_us alone. For trends_nyc only 178 days change in value, because 2899 of its 3653 raw days are exactly 0 and scaling leaves a zero at zero; its changed days are likewise confined to d1-7 (dom 1:22, 2:19, 3:26, 4:28, 5:29, 6:29, 7:25, and zero on d8-31). The structural defect — only days 1-7 rescaled — holds for both geos.

(c) MAGNITUDE IS PERIOD-DEPENDENT, and it is smallest where outcomes have already been seen. The quoted cai_d gap of -0.1019 SD is the full-decade figure. Split by window: discovery 2017-2020 gap = -0.0151 SD (2017-2019: -0.0616), and day-of-month dummies explain only R^2 = 0.007 of cai_d_lag0 there, not jointly significant (F p ~ 1.0). The FROZEN confirmation window (2015-16 + 2021-24) is where it bites: gap = -0.1598 SD. What is large and stable in every subperiod is the hard step at the day 7 -> 8 boundary: +0.181 SD (full decade), +0.174 (2017-2020), +0.211 (2017-2019), +0.186 (extension). So the practical consequence is not so much a threat to the already-examined discovery estimates as (i) a construct-validity defect — the anchoring step that the design doc credits with removing chain-stitch drift is inoperative on 77% of days, and the anchored series is a mixture of a monthly-window and a daily-window 0-100 normalisation — and (ii) a contamination of the treatment that is at its worst precisely in the confirmation sample, which is still blind and therefore still cheap to fix.

One further point the audit did not make: the "genuine day-of-month cycle in EMS mental-health calls" that the confounding story rests on is asserted from literature, not demonstrated in this repo — no built district-day panel exists under data/processed/ to test it against (only ems_pages/ raw shards). The confounding channel is plausible but unverified here; the construct-validity defect stands on its own.

Also note two internal contradictions in the same block: the docstring at :3-5 says "one un-stitched WEEKLY series ... rescaled so its weekly SUMS match the anchor", while the comment at :71 and the code at :75-77 match the anchor to the daily MEAN, not the sum.

title: The cai_d > 1.0 episode rule selects the top 22% of days in 2015 and the top 0.3% in 2024, because the two dominant components drift mechanically in opposite directions
fix: Detrend or within-year standardise each component before averaging (Algan et al.'s per-region zero-mean/unit-SD normalisation, cited by Hölzl et al. §4.2(4), is the analogue), or convert wiki_ext to a mean-per-article rather than a sum and express trends_us as a ratio to a stable benchmark term. Then define episodes by an equal within-year rate rather than a fixed level. Publish the diff against confirmation_episodes.csv per DATA_AUDIT §6 while outcomes are still blind.
claim: config.py:96 fixes EPISODE_Z_THRESHOLD = 1.0 on a standardised index whose within-year mean and SD move enormously across the panel. DATA_AUDIT §1 attributes this to component COUNT (SD 0.693-1.034 by count). The by-year picture is worse and has a different cause: wiki_ext is a SUM over a growing article set so its standardised mean rises monotonically, while trends_us is a relative search index whose denominator (total Google search volume) grows over the decade so its standardised mean falls monotonically. CAI-D's time profile is the partial cancellation of two opposed measurement drifts, and the fixed threshold slices it at a different percentile every year.
corrected_claim: The fixed rule `cai_d > 1.0` (scripts/config.py:96, applied at scripts/13_extension_episodes.py:23) does select a wildly different percentile of days in each year — 77.8th in 2015, 94.8th in 2018, 62.0th in 2020, 99.7th in 2024 — and this is decision-relevant because that day set becomes the frozen event list for the primary stacked event study (scripts/17_stacked_event_study.py:85). But the cause is not "two dominant components drifting in opposite directions". CAI-D is an unweighted mean of four components (12_build_cai.py:36, :82), three of them Google Trends series that all drift the same direction; annual mean cai_d correlates 0.79/0.89 with trends_us/trends_nyc and only 0.31 with wiki_ext, so the year profile is the trends bloc, not a cancellation. Neither component drifts monotonically: both peak in 2020 (wiki_ext +1.810, trends_us +0.855), so the year profile mixes real signal with whatever mechanical drift exists, and the drift mechanism for trends_us is asserted rather than demonstrated. Two distinct problems are in play, and DATA_AUDIT §1's component-count problem is the larger one for the pre-2017 years the claim emphasises: wiki_ext does not exist before 2015-07-01, and 66 of 2015's 81 high days fall in that wiki-absent half (mean cai_d +0.654 there vs -0.197 in the wiki-present half, 15 high days). The residual, genuinely new contribution is that composition alone does not explain everything: a fixed 2-component trends-only index, available on all 3,653 days, still runs from +0.648 (124 high days) in 2015 to -0.975 (2 high days) in 2024 — so DATA_AUDIT §1's "hold the component set fixed" remedy would not by itself equalise the by-year selection rate. Four supporting figures are wrong and should not be repeated: the pooled high-day rate is 10.35% (378/3653), not 6.2% (that is the audit's three-component-day rate), so an equal within-year rate is 37.8 days, not 23; 2015 contributes 12 episodes, not 8; and the post-2021 "starvation" does not hold at the episode level, where 2022 contributes 12 episodes — tied for the most in the panel — because near-threshold single days each become their own event.

title: Eight of the 40 extension episodes are artifacts of the Wikipedia coverage hole, and the episode labels that would have caught it are generated from the retired Twitter file
fix: Drop 2015-01-01..2015-06-30 from the analysis sample as DATA_AUDIT §3 already recommends, and state the resulting extension N (32 episodes, not 40). Replace the tweet_volume ranking in 13_extension_episodes.py:34-41 and 12_build_cai.py:137-142 with a source that exists over the whole decade - peak Wikipedia pageviews per victim, or peak GDELT coverage - and re-run the peak-alignment validation. For multi-week episodes, define rel_day 0 from the underlying killing/publicity date rather than from the threshold-crossing date.
claim: wiki_ext cannot begin before 2015-07-01 because the Wikimedia pageviews API begins there (11_fetch_awareness_components.py:7, :54; 21_refetch_wikipedia.py:49). For the first half of 2015 CAI-D is therefore the mean of only the Trends components - which are precisely the components whose standardised mean is highest in 2015 - so the index is mechanically elevated and generates episodes with no corresponding event. Separately, the attribution that would expose this is broken: 13_extension_episodes.py:34-41 ranks candidate victims by `tweet_volume` from wikipedia_article_resolution.csv, a field derived from the retired Twitter series and equal to 0 for every victim outside its top ~150, so most extension episodes are labelled with arbitrary names. The same code is duplicated in 12_build_cai.py:137-142, which is the "peak-alignment" check that AWARENESS_INDEX_DESIGN §4 relies on to validate the index.
corrected_claim:
Both halves of the finding hold, with one magnitude correction and one scope enlargement.

(a) The 2015 coverage hole. wiki_ext cannot begin before 2015-07-01 (11_fetch_awareness_components.py:7,:54; 21_refetch_wikipedia.py:49) and CAI-D is an NaN-skipping mean of available components (12_build_cai.py:82). 2015 H1 mean cai_d = +0.654 on 2.65 components vs H2 = -0.197 on 3.26; 66 of 2015's 81 high days are in H1; 8 of the 40 extension episodes start before 2015-07-01 with wiki_ext NaN. The upward direction is confirmed directly: in 2015 H2, where wiki_ext exists, its standardised mean is -1.704, and deleting it from that window moves mean cai_d -0.197 -> +0.506 and high days 15 -> 52. CORRECTION: imputing wiki_ext at that -1.704 level into H1 kills six of the eight episodes outright (ep1-5, ep8: zero high days, peaks 0.36-0.64), not eight. Episodes 6 and 7 survive as real events (Freddie Gray/Baltimore; June 2015) but with peaks inflated (3.93 -> 2.52; 2.32 -> 1.32) and start dates pulled early — ep6's first high day moves 2015-04-01 -> 2015-04-07, and since 17_stacked_event_study.py aligns rel_day 0 on `ep["start"]`, rel_day 0 for the longest 2015 episode still precedes Walter Scott's killing (registry 2015-04-04) and Freddie Gray's arrest (2015-04-12). So: six pure artifacts (15% of the extension sample) plus two real episodes with a mis-set event-time origin.

(b) The attribution defect, which is larger than stated. 13_extension_episodes.py:34-41 and its verbatim duplicate at 12_build_cai.py:137-142 rank candidate victims by `tweet_volume`, sourced from the retired Twitter panel (09_fetch_public_data.py:147-148, WIKI_TOP_N=150 at :83). The file holds 150 rows covering 147 of 13,144 registry victims (1.1%), with ZERO victims killed in 2021, 2022 or 2023 and one in 2024. Replaying the ranking: the prominence vector is entirely zero for 31 of 40 extension episodes and 8 of 30 discovery episodes (median 48 candidates per window), so the two printed names are just the first two registry rows in the window. Every 2021-2024 episode is affected — ep52 (Daunte Wright / Chauvin verdict) and ep65 (Tyre Nichols) are labelled with unrelated names because neither victim is in the file. DATA_AUDIT.md:159-163's "0 of 140 labels are out of window" certification cannot detect this, and AWARENESS_INDEX_DESIGN.md:42's peak-alignment validation runs on the same broken map.

The proposed fix is right, with one caveat: "drop 2015-01-01..2015-06-30" restates DATA_AUDIT.md:79-85, which already recommends it; the new contributions are the measured direction of the bias and the whole-decade scope of the attribution failure. Replacing tweet_volume with peak per-victim Wikipedia pageviews requires re-fetching that file too, since wikipedia_pageviews_victims.csv is itself built only for the same 150 Twitter-selected victims over 2017-2020 (09_fetch_public_data.py:191).

title: Wikipedia agent=user changed meaning in April 2020, non-retroactively, splitting the sample at the largest treatment episode; redirect accounting adds a second within-series break
fix: Refetch wiki_ext under agent=all-agents for the whole decade as a robustness series and report the correlation with the agent=user series and the ratio by period; or standardise wiki_ext separately within the pre-/post-April-2020 regimes. State the April 2020 break in the Methods with the WMF citation. Run 21_refetch_wikipedia.py to completion (the resolution file still shows the pre-fix state: Killing_of_Willie_McCoy 1 day, Killing_of_Eric_Garner 456 days) and, per Finding 5, convert wiki_ext from a sum to a per-article mean so article accumulation does not masquerade as attention.
claim: scripts/11_fetch_awareness_components.py:54 and scripts/21_refetch_wikipedia.py:88-89 request /all-access/user/. The Wikimedia Foundation documents that before April 2020 pageview classification had only "user" and "spider", that between 5% and 8% of 2019 English-Wikipedia desktop pageviews tagged "user" were actually bot spam, and that the new "automated" class introduced in April 2020 was NOT applied retroactively. The agent=user series therefore measures a systematically different quantity before and after April 2020 - and the standardisation window (2017-2019, 12_build_cai.py:39) lies entirely before the change while the largest episode (Floyd, 2020-05-26 to 2020-10-01) lies entirely after it. Wikimedia also counts hits on a redirect title separately from its target, so a page move creates two disjoint series with a step at the move date.
corrected_claim: The agent=user measurement break is real and correctly located, but its size is roughly an order of magnitude smaller than claimed where it matters most. The code does request /all-access/user/ (11_fetch_awareness_components.py:54, 21_refetch_wikipedia.py:88-89); the Wikimedia "automated" agent class was introduced in late April 2020 and was not applied retroactively (empirically: agent=automated is exactly 0 through 2019 and Jan-Mar 2020, first nonzero 2020-04-29 on every victim article tested); and the standardisation window (12_build_cai.py:39, 2017-2019) lies entirely before the break while the largest episode (2020-05-26..2020-10-01) lies entirely after it. However, the deflation is NOT 5-8% on these pages - that is WMF's aggregate 2019 English-Wikipedia desktop figure. Measured on the actual wiki_ext constituent titles, automated/(user+automated) is 0.4-0.5% during the Floyd episode, rising to 1.7-4.9% in late 2020 and 1.8-5.7% in 2021, so the break is largest in the extension window (2021-2024), not at Floyd. With SD of log1p(wiki_ext) = 0.6352 in the standardisation window, that is a z-shift of -0.008 SD at Floyd (-0.08 at 5%, -0.13 at 8%) against an episode mean wiki_ext z of 3.71; correcting for it moves CAI-D by 0.002-0.039 SD and flips 1-6 of 1,708 post-break days across the 1-SD episode threshold. It is therefore a Methods footnote, not a defect that changes any decision. The proposed fix is also wrong in direction: agent=all-agents adds spider traffic (~10% of user on these pages and unstable over time), so the correct robustness series is user+automated after April 2020 matched against user before. The rename/redirect half of the claim reproduces numerically in full but is already the documented DATA_AUDIT sec.3 defect that 21_refetch_wikipedia.py was written to fix.

title: The disposition filter deletes cancelled EDP dispatches: EDP-specific, 40x differential across families, 6x unstable in time, 40x across districts
fix: Retain disposition 87/CANCEL rows in the extract and make cancellation a reported outcome (edp_cancelled count and cancel rate) rather than a silent exclusion; run the primary specification with and without them as a pre-registered sensitivity. Correct or drop DUP and NOTSNT from the documented filter list. Report the EDP cancel rate by district-year in the QC table.
claim: 00_local_ems_extract.py:66 and 00b_download_ems_extract.py:73 drop dispositions {CANCEL, NOTSNT, DUP, 87}. The official dictionary (data/raw/EMS_incident_dispatch_data_description (1).xlsx, sheet 'Incident Dispositions') gives 87 = 'cancelled' and CANCEL = 'cancelled'. The pipeline therefore removes cancelled 911 calls -- the closest observable proxy for a caller who summoned help then thought better of summoning police, which is the study's own mechanism. The filter's bite is not constant: it is concentrated on EDP, moves 6x over time, and varies 40x across districts in a way aligned with the treated group in the DID and heterogeneity analyses.
corrected_claim:
CONFIRMED CORE, REFUTED CONSEQUENCES.

Every raw number in the finding reproduces against data/processed/ems_pages/*.parquet (14,500,000 rows). Verified: scripts/00_local_ems_extract.py:66 EXCLUDED_DISP_SQL = "('CANCEL','NOTSNT','DUP','87')" and scripts/00b_download_ems_extract.py:73 excl_disp = {"CANCEL","NOTSNT","DUP","87"}; the dictionary sheet 'Incident Dispositions' in data/raw/EMS_incident_dispatch_data_description (1).xlsx gives 87='cancelled', CANCEL='cancelled', DUP='duplicate incident', NOTSNT='unit not sent'. 2015 drop shares: EDP 10.390%, suicide_jump 10.090%, od_poison_drug 4.360%, asthma 2.119%, altmen 1.481% (injury 5.40% and cardiac 1.93% under my grouping vs the claim's 5.94/2.24 -- family-definition drift only). 2015 CANCEL rates: EDP 5.100% vs altmen 0.095%, cardiac 0.107%, asthma 0.147%, other 0.475%. Monthly EDP CANCEL: 0.76% (2012-02), 5.81% (2013-01), 8.58% (2015-06), 1.67% (2015-12), 0.85% (2016-05) -- exact. District range 2013-2016 over the 59 VALID_CDS: 0.24% (CD 503) to 11.73% (CD 203), Bronx 201-206 = 10.19-11.73%. Daily citywide 2013-2016: mean 3.60%, sd 3.87pp, max 26.90%; mean within-month sd 3.19pp vs sd of monthly means 1.76pp. DUP = 0 rows, NOTSNT = 173 rows. So the defect is real: the pipeline silently deletes cancelled EDP dispatches, its bite is EDP-specific and unstable in time and space, and the documented filter list (00_local_ems_extract.py:19-21) names a code (DUP) that never occurs.

Corrections that change what the finding is worth:

(1) The DID/heterogeneity alignment -- consequence (2), the finding's strongest confounding argument -- is FALSE. 07_did_exposure.py:45,48 defines treated as q_black==3 (top quartile pct_black_acs). Over 2013-2014 (chosen to stay outside every analysis and confirmation window), the 15 treated CDs average 2.98% EDP CANCEL versus 2.25% for the even-distribution control set (07_did_exposure.py:46,52) -- a 0.7pp gap, not a 40x one. Only CD 203 of the six high-cancel Bronx districts is in the treated group; 201, 202, 204, 205 and 206 are not top-quartile %Black. Quartile means are non-monotonic (Q1 1.55%, Q2 2.15%, Q3 6.16%, Q4 2.91%), and Spearman rho of cancel rate with pct_black is +0.39 against -0.82 with the borough-coded CD id. The spatial gradient tracks borough dispatch practice, not racial composition, which also weakens the reading of CANCEL as a caller-withdrawal proxy.

(2) The headline magnitude comparison is a category error. 0.22pp is an SD of an omitted outcome component; -0.00051 (docs/GATE2_PRELIMINARY_RESULTS.md:65) is a regression coefficient. Outcome variance uncorrelated with the regressor inflates SEs, it does not bias the estimate. Bias requires the cancel rate to covary with cai_d lags within CD x month_year (03_main_model.py:76), which the finding asserts but never shows.

(3) No evidence touches the estimation window. data/processed/ems_pages/page_014000000.parquet holds a full 500,000 rows, so the SODA paging loop in 00b terminated before exhausting the source; the extract spans 2005-01-01..2016-06-10 only. panel_cd_day.parquet and ems_cd_day_calltype.parquet do not exist on disk. There are zero EMS rows for ANALYSIS_START..ANALYSIS_END (2017-2020) or for the 2021-2024 confirmation window, so "straddles both confirmation windows" is unsupported for 2021-2024 and unknown for 2017-2020. The CANCEL surge is a bounded 2013-2015 regime that had already collapsed to 0.85-1.31% per month by spring 2016.

(4) Two descriptive overstatements. CANCEL is not "an almost exclusively EDP code": EDP is 33-45% of CANCEL rows by year. The correct statement is that EDP's CANCEL rate is 30-50x that of other call families. And code 87 -- not CANCEL -- is the larger filter by volume (547,637 rows vs 71,219), running a flat 5.3% of EDP calls every year 2005-2016 against 3.7% for other calls, so roughly half of EDP's 10.39% deletion is 87 and is stable, not the unstable CANCEL component. "DUP occurs zero times in 21 years" should read 11.4 years.

(5) One point the finding understates rather than overstates: the sign. Deleting cancelled EDP calls when attention rises pushes edp_share DOWN, the same direction as the hypothesis. The exposure is therefore a spurious-confirmation risk, not only an erasure of the mechanism.

Net: the fix as proposed (retain 87/CANCEL, report cancellation as an outcome, run a pre-registered with/without sensitivity, correct DUP and NOTSNT in the documented filter list, add EDP cancel rate by district-year to the QC table) is still worth doing, but it should be justified as measurement hygiene and construct-validity insurance, not as a demonstrated confound of the DID or heterogeneity results -- and it cannot be evaluated at all until the truncated EMS download is completed past 2016-06-10.

title: Two hard breaks sit inside the 2015-2016 confirmation window: geocoding completeness triples on 2016-01-01 and INJALS is retired on the peak day of confirmation episode 12
fix: Before opening the confirmation sample, add a break table to the QC output: per call code, first and last date observed and month-over-month step size; per year, the missing-communitydistrict rate. Then either add month_year FE to the event study or exclude episodes whose window crosses 2016-01-01, and exclude INJALS-era injury results from episodes 1-12.
claim: The 2015-2016 half of the confirmation sample straddles two discontinuities neither the panel builder nor the event study can see. (a) The rate of incidents with a NULL communitydistrict -- rows silently excluded by config.VALID_CDS at 01_build_panel.py:55 -- collapses from 2.9% to 0.9% at the start of 2016, mechanically inflating every district's denominator by roughly 2%. (b) INJALS, a member of the injury family at config.py:68, has its very last record on 2015-12-16 and zero thereafter; 2015-12-16 is the peak_date of confirmation episode 12 (2015-12-01..2015-12-18).
corrected_claim:
Two real, currently-unchecked discontinuities sit in the 2015-2016 confirmation window, but their effect on the H1 results is ~3 orders of magnitude smaller than the finding states, and neither can reach the reported test statistic.

(a) Geocoding completeness. The rate of EMS rows with a NULL communitydistrict falls from 3.12% (2015-11-01..12-18) to 0.63% (from 2016-01-14), with a two-stage transition; the best single break date by SSR is 2015-12-31. Annual rates reproduce exactly: 2.087% (2014), 2.969% (2015), 0.774% (2016 H1). Missingness is call-type differential (2015: injury 4.79%, suicide_jump 9.75%, edp 2.87%, altmen 1.42%). These rows are dropped at scripts/00b_download_ems_extract.py:88 -- pandas groupby drops NaN keys -- not at 01_build_panel.py:55, so they never enter even the pct_calls_in_dropped_pseudo_districts QC metric. IMPACT: the proportional denominator change cancels in a share; only the differential bites. Share-among-geocoded exceeds share-among-all by 0.036pp in 2015 and 0.014pp in 2016 post-break, so the induced step in mh_narrow_share is 0.00022, not 0.0018 -- about 0.4x the reported effect (0.0005-0.0007), not 3x.

(b) INJALS retirement. Confirmed: 10,371 records, 2013-12-09 12:09:37 to 2015-12-16 11:41:03, 292 in 2015-12, zero thereafter; 2015-12-16 is episode 12's peak_date. INJALS was 2.4-2.7% of the injury family (0.47pp of 19.2pp of all calls), not 1.5%, and the retirement is partly a within-family recode (INJMAJ rises 2.93% -> 3.07% of all valid-CD calls across the boundary) with the geocoding change pushing injury share the other way.

REACHABILITY (the part that changes the decision): the H1 statistic is the mean of rel_day 0..7 coefficients (scripts/event_study.py:79-97). For episode 12 that is 2015-12-01..12-08. EVENT_WINDOW_POST=14 ends the primary window at rel_day +14 = 2015-12-15, when INJALS is still present. INJALS retires at rel_day +15, the geocoding transition falls at rel_day +30..+44 -- both outside the primary window and outside the 0..7 statistic even under the 28/60 sensitivities, where they leak in only through the episode-12 ep_cd fixed effect (order 3e-6 on mh_narrow_share). Only episode 12 straddles either break; episodes 1-11 sit wholly inside the INJALS era and their episode-level levels are absorbed by ep_cd FE.

APPROPRIATE FIX: add the break table to QC (per call code first/last date and month-over-month step; per-year missing-communitydistrict rate) -- it is genuinely absent from 20_data_audit.py and cheap. Flag episode 12's long-window (28/60) injury-channel results as sensitive to the INJALS retirement. Do not add month_year FE or drop episodes on account of the geocoding break; the measured artifact is 0.00022 on mh_narrow_share and cannot reach the first-week statistic.

title: EDPM is born on the exact day B-HEARD launches, and T-EDP is born inside the largest discovery episode
fix: Verify against FDNY documentation what EDPM denotes and whether it is the B-HEARD routing code; if so, report the outcome with and without EDPM for 2021+ and state the choice in the pre-registration. Report T-EDP separately rather than silently inside the family (it is ~0.2% of the family, so exclusion is cheap). Replace the config.py:57-59 comment with the actual annual family totals.
claim: config.py:60 folds EDPM and T-EDP into the edp family. Their birth dates are not neutral. EDPM's first record is 2021-06-03; config.py:109 sets BHEARD_LAUNCH = 2021-06-01. The code the pipeline uses to keep the EDP family whole across the B-HEARD transition was created by that transition -- outcome definition and confound share a birthday. T-EDP's first record is 2020-06-05, eleven days after George Floyd's killing and inside episode 45's window: a call-type code whose existence is plausibly caused by the treatment, the same failure mode already documented for trends_victims in DATA_AUDIT.md §2.
corrected_claim:
The EDP family definition in scripts/config.py:53-60 rests on two false comments and omits two live codes; the alleged contamination mechanisms do not hold.

CONFIRMED. Every number reproduces exactly against SODA 76xm-jjuj: EDPC 2018-07-06T16:42:55 (484,960), EDPM 2021-06-03T15:16:58 (125,308), T-EDP 2020-06-05T02:37:24 (3,487), EDPW 2018-10-28T18:19:25 (226); the 2021-05/06 split (EDP 7,874→5,479, EDPC 4,828→4,963, EDPM 0→1,638); T-EDP 2020 monthly 7/23/21/16/24/28/23; annual family totals 108,384 (2016) through 141,910 (2024), a 47% range that matches "~125k" only in 2017-2018. The config.py:57-59 parenthetical "family total stable ~125k/yr" is therefore false, and it is the stated justification for the grouping. Additionally, config.py:53-54 claims the codes come from the official dictionary sheet "Call Type Descriptions", but that sheet (data/raw/EMS_incident_dispatch_data_description (1).xlsx, 271 codes) contains only "EDP" = PSYCHIATRIC PATIENT — EDPC, EDPM, EDPW and T-EDP are all undocumented, and edp is the only group in CALL_TYPE_GROUPS with undocumented members.

REFUTED. EDPM is not the B-HEARD routing code. In June 2021 it appears citywide (top precincts 103 n=47, 42 n=46, 25 n=44, 73 n=44, 75 n=43); the three pilot precincts 25/28/32 hold 113 of 1,638 EDPM calls (6.9%), an 18.8% within-family share against 13.5% citywide, and their family total is flat May→June (624→601) against a citywide -4.8%. The confound is not pre-absorbed into the outcome and the B-HEARD control does not double-count. T-EDP is likewise not treatment-caused: it is one of twenty "T-" codes born together in mid-2020 (T-DFBR 06-02, T-TEXT 06-02, T-ARST 06-03, T-SICK 06-04, T-EDP 06-05, T-TRMA 06-05, T-INJ 06-08, T-CARD 07-12, T-ASTH 11-02, ...), an FDNY-wide telehealth/triage rollout that also hits the placebo groups. It is numerically inert in discovery: 68 of 48,884 family calls in episode 45's window (0.14%), and all T- codes together are 512 of 473,606 calls there (0.11%). The title's "exact day" is also off by two days, and BHEARD_LAUNCH is a first-of-month convention (adoption_earliest 2021-06-01 / latest 2021-06-30).

MISSED, AND MORE CONSEQUENTIAL. EDPE (from 2024-04-10; 2,030 in 2024) and EDPT (from 2023-03-01; 2,525 in 2023, 4,045 in 2024) exist in the data and are absent from config.py:60. Unmapped codes fall to "other" (01_build_panel.py:52), entering total_calls but no numerator, so the EDP-family share is understated by ~4.3% relative in 2024 and growing — the exact time-trending undercount config.py:59 says the family exists to prevent, sitting inside the 2021-2024 confirmation sample. The same applies to the T- codes against the cardiac, asthma, injury and altmen groups.

URGENCY. 01_build_panel.py:43 restricts the panel to 2016-12-01..2021-01-31, so no EDPM, EDPE or EDPT record is in any current estimate, and no estimation script reads bheard_cd_exposure.csv. This is a pre-registration blocker for the confirmation rebuild, not a defect in a produced result.

FIX. Replace the config.py:57-59 parenthetical with the actual annual totals and with the EDPC evidence that does hold (July 2018 onward). Correct config.py:53-54 to say four of the five edp codes are undocumented in the shipped dictionary. Decide and pre-register the treatment of EDPE and EDPT (and of the T- codes across all groups) before the confirmation panel is rebuilt. Reporting the outcome with and without EDPM for 2021+ remains a cheap sensitivity, but no longer as a B-HEARD contamination fix; T-EDP can stay in the family, since excluding it on treatment-endogeneity grounds is not warranted.

claim: 00b_download_ems_extract.py:88 aggregates with groupby(["incident_date","communitydistrict","final_call_type"]), and pandas drops NaN group keys by default (verified on the installed pandas 3.0.5). corrected_claim: 00b_download_ems_extract.py:88 groups on ["incident_date","communitydistrict","final_call_type"] after coercing communitydistrict with pd.to_numeric(errors="coerce") at :83, and pandas 3.0.5 drops NaN group keys by default (verified: 4-row frame with 2 NaN CDs yields 2 groups, 4 with dropna=False). title: The ratified "precondition" null calibration is vacuous as run, was not calibrated to the real panel, and its own stated failure mode is never tested
fix: Re-run with at least the default 200 sims x 200 draws after panel_cd_day.parquet exists so rho/sigma/mu come from the real panel, add a Kolmogorov-Smirnov uniformity test on the p-values to the VERDICT (not just the rejection rate), and record the fitted rho in the memo. claim: docs/GATE_C_MEMO.md §3 and §6.3 make the synthetic-null calibration "a precondition, not a robustness column", and 18_null_calibration.py's docstring (lines 3-5, 23-27) says the confirmatory run should not happen if it fails, naming two failure modes: over-rejection, and "p-values piled at 0 or 1 rather than uniform". The committed run used --sims 12 --draws 25 against defaults of 200/200, ar1_rho stayed at the 0.6 fallback (18:53,67,83) meaning panel_cd_day.parquet was absent so the AR(1) was NOT estimated from the real data, and the VERDICT logic at 18:127-131 tests only the rejection rate — uniformity is never tested despite being a documented failure mode.

Every factual element reproduces: outputs/tables/null_calibration.csv records n_sims_completed=12, ri_draws_per_sim=25, ar1_rho=0.6, empirical_rejection_rate=0.0, band [-0.0733, 0.1733], median_p=0.7142, VERDICT=CALIBRATED, against defaults of 200/200 (18:51-53); data/processed/ contains no panel_cd_day.parquet, so 18:69-83 took the uncalibrated else-branch; and the VERDICT at 18:127-131 tests only the rejection rate while the docstring's second failure mode (18:27, "p-values piled at 0 or 1") is never tested (median_p is written at 18:141 but unused). THREE FACTS RAISE SEVERITY BEYOND THE ORIGINAL CLAIM. (1) The reduced sim count did not merely make the check uninformative — it converted a FAIL into a PASS. The band is alpha +/- 1.96*sqrt(alpha(1-alpha)/n) (18:129-130), so lo <= 0 whenever n < 73; at n=12 lo=-0.0733, but at the ratified default n=200 lo=+0.0198, and the observed rejection rate of 0.0 would have printed "NOT CALIBRATED - UNDER-rejects" (18:155-158), which per the script blocks the confirmatory run. (2) At n=12 the under-rejection branch is mathematically unreachable: only rej > 0.1733 (>=3 of 12 sims) can fail, so the failure mode actually present cannot be detected. (3) Each sim used only 24-25 valid RI draws (confirmed in the reproduction), giving p-value resolution 0.04, so p<0.05 requires <=1 of 25 null draws to exceed |obs| and a nominal 5% test is barely representable. title: trends_nyc has a ~2.8x artificial level break on 2021-09-26 caused by the stitching scale fallback — it sits inside the frozen confirmation window
fix: Replace the ratio-of-means chain with a robust link (regress new on previous over the overlap through the origin, require a minimum number of jointly-positive overlap days, and abort loudly instead of falling back to 1.0). Re-anchor the whole NYC series to the un-stitched decade anchor. Then rebuild the episode list and publish the diff for 2021-2024.
claim: scripts/11b_fetch_trends.py:53 falls back to `scale = 1.0` whenever the overlap mean of the new chunk is zero. The NYC chunk covering 2021-05-29..2021-09-25 is entirely zero, so both overlap means were 0 and the chain reset: from 2021-09-26 onward the NYC series sits on the raw 0-100 scale of a fresh window rather than on the 2015-2021 chain. The break survives 11c because the anchoring only touches days 1-7 (finding 1).
corrected_claim:
trends_nyc has an artificial multiplicative level break beginning 2021-09-26, caused by the `else 1.0` scale fallback at scripts/11b_fetch_trends.py:53. The mechanism, the break date, and the downstream damage are all confirmed; only the size of the break is misstated — it is roughly 4x, not 2.8x.

Verified mechanism: chunk 19's exclusive segment (2021-05-29..2021-09-25) is entirely zero, so prev_m = 0 at the 19->20 link. Since the post-break series is not identically zero, new_m must also have been 0, so `scale` fell back to 1.0 and chunk 20 onward sits on the raw 0-100 scale of a fresh window instead of the 2015-2021 chain. Per-chunk quantization units confirm this: ~11-19 for chunks 0-18, then 65, 48.9, 64.11, 73, 70.55, 63.28, 69.94, 76.77, 153, 97 for chunks 20-29. trends_us shows no such break, so it is NYC-specific.

The break survives 11c because the "weekly" anchor request at 11c:62 spans 10 years and Trends returns MONTHLY data for such a window; the 7-day mask at 11c:74 therefore rescales only days 1-7 of each month. Only 178 of 3653 NYC days differ between the stitched and anchored files, and all of them are days 1-7.

Corrected magnitude: the claim's "mean(stitched/anchor) = 0.578 pre vs 1.601 post, factor 2.77" does not reproduce. Recovering the monthly anchor from the anchored days 1-7, I get 0.6951 pre (56 months) vs 3.2397 post (15 months) = 4.661 at month level, 3.964 at day level, 3.312 pooled. A cleaner year-by-year measure — the ratio of stitched days 8-31 to anchored days 1-7 — is stable at 0.52-0.97 for 2015-2021 and jumps to 2.674 (2022), 3.451 (2023), 1.816 (2024), against a trends_us ratio that is flat at 1.09-1.37 in all ten years. So the inflation is roughly 2.6x-5x, averaging about 4x.

Corrected downstream impact (deflating only days 8-31, since days 1-7 are already on the anchor scale): 2022's share of days with cai_d > 1.0 falls from 0.0438 to 0.0110 (not 0.022) and its episode count from 12 to 4 (not 7); 2023 falls from 0.0438 to 0.0301 and 5 episodes to 2; total episodes 70 -> 58. The claim's stated figures (0.044 -> 0.022 and 0.044 -> 0.027) reproduce exactly under its own 2.77x assumption, so its arithmetic is internally consistent — the assumption is just too conservative.

Two facts make this more damaging than the claim states. First, all 16 of 2022's threshold-crossing days are driven by trends_nyc alone (z = 2.40-3.00, while trends_us z is -0.37 to 1.10), and all 16 fall on days 8-31, i.e. entirely on the un-anchored scale. Second, NYC attention on the true anchor scale did not rise in 2022 at all: the anchored days-1-7 annual mean is 2.50 in 2021, 2.17 in 2022, 3.42 in 2023. The entire apparent 2022 attention signal in the frozen episode list is artifactual.

Note also that docs/DATA_AUDIT.md:13-31 already flags 2022's 12 episodes but blames component-count instability; that attribution is wrong, since correcting the NYC scale alone with the component set held fixed removes two thirds of them.

The latent bug is real as described: with prev_m == 0 and new_m > 0, `scale` evaluates to 0.0 and every subsequent chunk is multiplied to zero permanently.

title: trends_victims is not in "topic units" — the code never divides by the topic term, so every sizeable victim saturates at exactly 100 and the component counts open windows rather than measuring attention

claim: The docstring (11c:7-10) claims victim volume is "expressed in topic-term units and is therefore comparable across victims". The code does not do this: line 96 is `ratio = df[name].astype(float)` — the victim column is taken raw, never divided by `df[TOPIC]`. The variable name says a ratio was intended. Because Google Trends normalises a multi-term window so that max over ALL terms = 100, any victim whose peak exceeds the topic term's peak in that window is pinned to 100 regardless of true magnitude, and the pinning threshold moves with the topic term's own level, which varies ~4x across the decade.

title: trends_nyc is a censored indicator, not a level: 79% of days are exactly zero and the censoring rate swings from 55% (2020) to 98% (2024)
fix: Do not treat NYC zeros as levels. Either (a) fetch the NYC series with a broader term set or as a topic so it clears the floor, (b) model trends_nyc as a censored variable / binary above-floor indicator, or (c) drop it from CAI-D and demote it to a validation exhibit. Report the zero-share by year in the Methods table whichever route is taken.
claim: The NYC-DMA daily series for the literal term "police brutality" is below Google's reporting floor on most days, so it is recorded as 0. Zero is not "no attention"; it is "below the floor of THIS window's 0-100 rescaling", and that floor moves with the window's maximum. The censoring rate is itself a function of attention intensity and of which spike happened to fall in the same 180-day window, so the component means something different in every year.
corrected_claim:
CONFIRMED with one framing correction and additional aggravating evidence.

All quantitative evidence reproduces exactly. trends_nyc in data/reference/cai_trends_daily.csv is 0 on 2899 of 3653 days (0.7936); yearly zero-shares are 0.6630, 0.7186, 0.7534, 0.7836, 0.7507, 0.5519, 0.9205, 0.9205, 0.8904, 0.9836. The anchored file cai_trends_anchored.csv (the one scripts/12_build_cai.py:47-51 actually loads) has the identical zero pattern. In data/processed/cai_daily.parquet all 2899 zero days carry the single value trends_nyc = -0.554082, analytically (0 - 0.7333)/1.3234 from the 2017-2019 log1p mean/SD; that one constant is 79.36% of the series. The 2017-2019 standardisation window is 762/1095 = 76.26% zeros. Yearly corr(trends_us_z, trends_nyc_z) is 0.635/0.541/0.487/0.326/0.422/0.732/0.432/0.233/0.418/0.054 against a full-sample 0.535 reported as corr_nyc_vs_us_trends (row 17, 0-indexed, outputs/tables/cai_validation.csv). The anchor figures also reproduce: 49 of 120 months, 8 in 2021, 8 in 2022, 10 in 2024.

STRONGER DIRECT PROOF THAN OFFERED: in the first un-stitched 180-day chunk (2015-01-01..2015-06-29) the raw integer NYC values have distinct set [0, 19, 20, 21, ...] with nothing between 1 and 18. A recorded 0 therefore means "anywhere in [0,18] on this window's 0-100 scale", i.e. up to 18% of the window maximum. Zero is a censoring bin whose width is set by the window, exactly as claimed. Chunk-level zero-share of newly assigned days swings from 0.233 (chunk 2020-04-04..2020-09-30, containing Floyd) to 1.000 (chunk 2021-03-30..2021-09-25, all 120 newly assigned days exactly 0). Longest consecutive zero run is 153 days, 2024-05-14 to 2024-10-13.

THREE AGGRAVATING FACTS THE FINDING DID NOT REPORT:
(1) scripts/11c_trends_anchor_and_victims.py:62 requests the timeframe "2015-01-01 2024-12-31" in one call, which Google Trends returns at MONTHLY granularity, but line 73 builds the rescale mask as wstart to wstart+7 days. The anchor therefore rescales only days 1-7 of each month; days 8-31 are bit-identical to the unstitched stitched series (verified: share identical to stitched is 1.000 for every day-of-month >= 8 and ~0.00 for days 1-7 in trends_us). The drift-correction step the design relies on is inert for 76% of days. Relatedly, the anchor series is never persisted, so the "49 of 120 months" figure is not independently verifiable from stored artifacts: all 49 are months in which the stitched days 1-7 were also all zero, so anchor=0 cannot be distinguished from the no-rescale branch (m>0 guard).
(2) scripts/20_data_audit.py:78 lists trends_nyc in ALWAYS_ON and uses that trio as the clean reference baseline for trends_victims_selection_gap and corr_cai_d_vs_always_on_only; outputs/tables/data_audit.csv grades it "coverage_trends_nyc, 2015-01-01..2024-12-31, PASS, 3653 days, 0 internal gaps" — the exact error class under audit.
(3) scripts/13_extension_episodes.py:23 derives all 70 episodes (40 of them extension-period, including 2021-2024) directly from cai_d > 1.0, so the censoring propagates straight into the frozen confirmation-window event definitions.

FRAMING CORRECTION: the weights are not a clean 3/4-national + 1/4-local in discovery versus national in confirmation. trends_victims is absent for all 366 days of 2024 and 361 of 365 days of 2022, so trends_nyc carries 1/3 weight there — but it also carries 1/3 weight on 347 of 365 days of 2017, inside the discovery window (mean n_d_components: 2017 = 3.05, 2018 = 3.74, 2024 = 3.00). And 2015-2016, which are confirmation-window years, are the LEAST censored in the decade (66.3% and 71.9%). The proposed fix is unaffected.

title: The CAI-S divergence-day falsification sample is selected by component count, not by supply/demand divergence
fix: Restrict the divergence test to 2017-2022 where both supply components exist, or standardise cai_s after averaging so that component count cannot drive the tail. Re-derive the divergence day list and re-check how many days survive.
claim: cai_s is the unweighted mean of whatever supply components exist (12_build_cai.py:83). gdelt_news covers only 2017-2022, so cai_s is a single-component index in 2015, 2016, 2023 and for 81 days of 2024, and a two-component (variance-halved) index elsewhere. The divergence test (12_build_cai.py:148) selects days with cai_s above its own 95th percentile, which mechanically selects the single-component years.
corrected_claim:
The CAI-S divergence-day falsification test is vacuous, but because gdelt_tv is not comparable across years — not because of component count.

Verified as stated: cai_s is the unweighted mean of available supply components (12_build_cai.py:83); gdelt_news exists only 2017-2022; the divergence rule (12_build_cai.py:148) yields 18 days, 17 of them in years where gdelt_news is missing; all quoted SDs and the 0.756 correlation reproduce exactly.

The attributed mechanism is wrong. At r = 0.756 averaging two components reduces SD by 6%, not by half; measured in the six years where both exist, SD(cai_s)/SD(gdelt_tv) averages 0.915 and exceeds 1 in 2020. A counterfactual that holds component count constant at one in every year (gdelt_tv alone as the supply index, same selection rule) still returns 12 days in 2015, 3 in 2016 and 3 in 2023 out of 25 — the year concentration survives removing the alleged cause entirely, and the two-component average is in fact what admits the 2017-2019/2022 days the as-built version lacks.

The real defect is that gdelt_tv means something different before 2017: raw annual mean 0.09 (2015) and 0.06 (2016) versus 0.03/0.02/0.02 in 2017-2019, with only 36.4%/62.0% zero-days versus 68-76%. Because all components are standardised on the 2017-2019 window (12_build_cai.py:77-78), the denser pre-window series is pushed into the upper tail by construction. This is the same error class the audit targets, but the object is gdelt_tv's cross-year comparability, not the number of components averaged.

Neither proposed fix works. Standardising cai_s after averaging is a strict no-op — a global affine transform against a within-sample quantile leaves the selected day set bit-identical (verified, 18 == 18). Restricting to 2017-2022 leaves exactly 1 divergence day (2021-12-28), so the fix does not repair the test; it retires it.

Correct action: do not report the divergence day list as a passed falsification check. Either drop the test, or rebuild it on a supply series whose level and density are stable across 2015-2024, and separately flag gdelt_tv's pre-2017 level break wherever else it enters. (Minor: in 2024 cai_s is single-component on 285 days and undefined on 81, not single-component on 81.)

title: The Trends "weekly anchor" is actually MONTHLY, so only days 1-7 of each month were rescaled — the other 77% of days keep the stitched scale
fix: Re-fetch the anchor at weekly granularity by requesting it in <5-year blocks (Trends returns weekly for 1-5 year windows) and chaining those, or drop the anchoring step entirely and keep the pure stitched series (the drift check below shows US stitching is sound). If the monthly anchor is kept, the mask must span the actual period each anchor point covers (`wstart` to the next `wstart`), not a hard-coded 7 days. Until fixed, add day-of-month fixed effects to every model and re-derive the episode list; report the diff.
claim: scripts/11c_trends_anchor_and_victims.py:61 requests a single Trends series over `"2015-01-01 2024-12-31"`. Google Trends returns MONTHLY granularity for a 10-year window, not weekly as the docstring (11c:3-6) and the loop assume. Line 74 then applies a 7-day mask (`anchored.index < wstart + pd.Timedelta(days=7)`) to what are month-start timestamps, so only days 1-7 of each month get rescaled to the anchor; days 8-31 retain the 11b chain-stitched scale, which is a systematically different scale. The result is a permanent within-month step in the treatment.
corrected_claim:
scripts/11c_trends_anchor_and_victims.py:61 requests the Trends anchor over a 10-year window, which Google returns at MONTHLY granularity, not weekly as the docstring (11c:3-5) and the 7-day mask at 11c:74 assume. Confirmed from the committed data: backing the anchor out of data/reference/cai_trends_anchored.csv yields exactly 120 values, one per calendar month, all integers on 0-100 with max exactly 100.0 in 2020-06. Consequently only days 1-7 of each month are rescaled — anchored/stitched is exactly 1.000 for all 2777 trends_us days with day-of-month > 7 (sd 1.79e-17) and ranges 0.337-3.642 on the 834 days 1-7. The anchoring step is therefore inoperative for 77% of the series, and because the anchor scale sits ~25% below the stitched scale (yearly median anchor / full-month-mean stitched = 0.774, 0.742, 0.746, 0.765, 0.737, 0.741, 0.730, 0.786, 0.747, 0.715 for 2015-2024), it leaves a permanent within-month step: trends_us mean z = -0.447 on days 1-7 vs -0.039 on days 8+ (-0.408 SD, p=3.5e-16), 8 of 10 years at p<0.001. The script's own diagnostic (11c:80-81), corr(stitched, anchored) = 0.886 / 0.908, hides it.

The downstream consequence is narrower than originally stated. (a) In the frozen discovery window the composite treatment is clean: cai_d step is -0.0151 SD, t=-0.24, p=0.8135 over 2017-2020, versus -0.1019, t=-2.95, p=0.0032 over the full decade — the composite averages the contaminated trends_us with 2-3 uncontaminated components, and the years carrying the step (2015, 2016, 2021-2024) are exactly the ones not yet examined. So 03_main_model.py's missing day-of-month FE is not a live problem for the discovery estimates. (b) The event-study sub-claim is wrong: 17_stacked_event_study.py:85-89 stacks on episode `start`, and starts are uniform in the month (15 of 70 on days 1-7 vs 16.1 expected, p=0.887). Only `peak_date` is skewed (8 of 70, p=0.022), and peak_date is used only in 08_figures.py:51 and 20_data_audit.py:171, never in estimation. (c) Day-of-month explains only 0.7% of cai_d variance (joint F p=0.685) and 2.2% of trends_us — a 1-df step, not a broad sawtooth. (d) The asserted benefit-payment cycle in the outcome could not be checked: data/processed/panel_cd_day.parquet is absent from this checkout.

Correct disposition: fix the anchor (re-fetch in <5-year blocks for weekly granularity, or mask wstart-to-next-wstart instead of a hard-coded 7 days, or drop anchoring and keep the stitched series) BEFORE unfreezing 2015-2016 and 2021-2024, since that is where the contamination lives. Add a day-of-month FE robustness check rather than changing every model's specification, and re-derive the episode list after the fix. No re-estimation of the 2017-2020 discovery results is required on account of this defect.

title: Trends measurement precision degrades ~5x over the decade, so treatment attenuation bias is year-specific and a 2021-2024 null is not interpretable

Then report a per-year signal-to-quantization diagnostic, and pre-specify an attenuation-corrected or reliability-weighted specification before opening the confirmation sample.
claim: Google Trends returns integers 0-100 rescaled to each request window's own maximum. Because US search share for "police brutality" falls sharply over the decade while the request windows are fixed at 180 days, the number of distinct values the daily series can take collapses toward the end of the sample. The treatment therefore carries far more quantization error in 2021-2024 than in 2015-2019 — classical measurement error that attenuates the coefficient by a year-varying factor.
corrected_claim: Google Trends does rescale each 180-day request window to that window's own max, but that is precisely why the decade-long decline in search level does NOT reduce daily resolution: every window still spans raw 0-100. Reconstructing the quantization unit for all 30 chunks of data/reference/cai_trends_daily.csv confirms trends_us hits an implied raw max of ~100 in essentially every chunk from 2015 through 2024, and its precision is flat over the decade (relative quantization step 0.0360 in 2015-2019 vs 0.0373 in 2021-2024, ratio 1.04x; distinct values per chunk 48.6 vs 44.6; standardised SD 0.98-1.01 vs 0.90-1.12). The finding's per-chunk raw-max table (25.0/14.0/16.7 in 2015, 5.0/3.8 in 2021-22) does not reproduce and is impossible by construction. What actually drives coarseness is within-window peakiness (corr = +0.978 with log peakiness, -0.04 with year), so the coarsest US window in the sample is 2020-02-04..2020-06-02 (12 distinct values over 120 days) — inside the discovery window, not the confirmation window. The precision problem is real but confined to trends_nyc, and it is zero-censoring rather than range compression: non-zero days fall from 123/103/90/79/91 in 2015-2019 to 29/29/40/6 in 2021-2024, with a 153-day all-zero run and all of 2021-05-29..2021-09-25 zero; in 2024 trends_nyc is non-zero on 6 of 366 days and takes 7 distinct values, making it a near-constant in the composite. That is one of three components live in 2024 (trends_victims is 0/366), it is not a 5x decade-wide attenuation of the treatment, and docs/DATA_AUDIT.md:37-48 conceals it by recording trends_nyc availability as 1.00 in every year. The right remedy is a zero-inflation / informative-days diagnostic per component-year and a decision rule for dropping or reweighting trends_nyc when its non-zero share collapses — not a decade-wide attenuation correction.

title: trends_victims' standardisation constants are estimated on a treatment-selected 39% subsample of the reference window

corrected_claim:
scripts/12_build_cai.py:74-78 standardises each CAI-D component separately on 2017-2019 using only that component's observed days. For trends_victims the zero point and scale are estimated from 431 of 1095 reference days (39.4%; ref mean(log1p)=0.561, sd=0.984), versus all 1095 for wiki_ext, trends_us and trends_nyc. This is a genuine apples-to-oranges scale mismatch: trends_victims' zero point means "a typical day on which Google Trends reported the series", while the other three mean "a typical calendar day". However the consequences are the opposite of those originally asserted.

(a) The bias is conservative, not inflationary. Centring on a higher-mean subsample pulls z-scores down, so trends_victims' z averages only +0.090 on observed days (+0.023 into the 4-component mean) versus +0.635 (+0.159) under a full-window calibration imputing below-floor days as zero; CAI-D on those days is +0.296 as built versus +0.436. The selective calibration partly OFFSETS the DATA_AUDIT section 2 availability effect by about 0.14 CAI-D units rather than compounding it.

(b) trends_victims is the LEAST reference-window-sensitive of the four components, not the most: shifting to a 2021-2023 window moves its z by mean 0.179 versus 0.343 for trends_nyc, 0.727 for wiki_ext and 0.770 for trends_us (same ordering for 2017-2018, 2018-2019, 2016-2019). A reference-window robustness check would implicate wiki_ext's growth trend (DATA_AUDIT section 1), not this component.

(c) Within the reference window the subsample is only mildly attention-selected: +0.104 SD on the other three components, not the +0.593 SD full-panel gap, which is driven by between-year composition. And 61% of the reference days Trends does report are exact zeros, so availability is not a simple value floor.
